title: Manchester United vs AC Milan – Predicted lineup and team news
description: Manchester United will face AC Milan in their final pre-season match on Saturday at the Tarczynsky Arena in Poland.United head into this last warm-up showing reasonably consistent form under Michael C...
fullText:
Manchester United will face AC Milan in their final pre-season match on Saturday at the Tarczynsky Arena in Poland.

United head into this last warm-up showing reasonably consistent form under Michael Carrick, with two wins, two draws and one loss. After an opening 1-0 defeat by Wrexham, they recovered to beat Rosenborg 5-0 and Atlético Madrid 2-1.

They then had back-to-back 1-1 draws with Paris Saint-Germain and Leeds United, although they beat Leeds 5-4 on penalties to lift the BoyleSports Cup.

Carrick has named a 26-man squad for the trip to Poland, and there are notable returns.

Marcus Rashford is poised to appear for the first time in 20 months after completing his reintegration into first-team training.

Lisandro Martínez and Kobbie Mainoo have both returned to full training and are likely to get their first pre-season minutes from the bench, while Bruno Fernandes should begin rebuilding his match fitness in the starting lineup.

However, United are missing several key players through injury. Benjamin Šeško will miss the tour entirely with a shin injury, while Mason Mount and Manuel Ugarte are out with foot and knee problems respectively.

Matthijs de Ligt is still recovering from major back surgery, and Tom Heaton's hamstring issue means Senne Lammens will start in goal.

Possible Manchester United starting XI: Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo

The match will kick off at 3:45pm BST on Saturday, 15th August.

In the UK, the friendly between Manchester United and AC Milan will be shown live exclusively on MUTV.

title: Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen – Predicted lineup and team news

fullText:
Newcastle host German side Bayer Leverkusen at St James' Park on Saturday in one of their final pre-season friendlies before the Premier League begins next week.

The Magpies' preparation has been uneven. They beat Darlington 3-0 and Valencia 2-1, but have struggled as Matthias Jaissle implements his changes. Newcastle were hammered 4-1 by Bristol City and arrive at today's game after a disappointing 3-1 reverse to Everton, exposing defensive frailties and problems in front of goal.

Newcastle have a mix of injury returns and ongoing issues. Fabian Schär and Lewis Miley are progressing well from groin and fibula injuries respectively and could make brief appearances today as they near full fitness.

Tino Livramento, however, remains out with a serious calf and knee ligament problem and is undergoing rehab in the United States, ruling him out of the Premier League opener.

Left-back Lewis Hall is a late fitness doubt after a minor knock, which would leave Dylan Charlton ready to step in.

Up front, new summer signing Bazoumana Touré is likely to start on the left wing, while Anthony Elanga has recovered from a recent scare and should feature on the right.

This match is an important chance to further integrate the squad following the high-profile summer exits of Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimarães.

Possible Newcastle starting XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Charlton; Bamba, Joelinton; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

title: Manchester United vs AC Milan – Match preview and team news
description: Manchester United is set to meet AC Milan in their final pre-season match on Saturday at the Tarczynsky Arena in Poland.Manchester United vs AC Milan – Match preview and team newsDate: Saturday, 15...
fullText:
Manchester United is set to meet AC Milan in their final pre-season match on Saturday at the Tarczynsky Arena in Poland.

Venue: Tarczynsky Arena, Wroclaw, Poland.

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has named a 26-man travelling squad for the pre-season fixture in Poland, highlighted by several major selection boosts.

Marcus Rashford is set to make his first appearance for the club in 20 months after successfully reintegrating into first-team training.

Furthermore, vital duo Lisandro Martínez and Kobbie Mainoo have returned to full training and are expected to earn their first minutes of pre-season from the substitutes' bench, while playmaker Bruno Fernandes should start to build match sharpness.

However, United face several high-profile injury absences. Star striker Benjamin Šeško completely misses the tour due to a shin injury, while midfielders Mason Mount and Manuel Ugarte remain sidelined with foot and knee knocks.

Additionally, defender Matthijs de Ligt is still recovering from major back surgery, and goalkeeper Tom Heaton's hamstring issue hands Senne Lammens a starting opportunity.

AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim faces a severe squad crisis ahead of this high-profile reunion against his former club, with up to eight senior players unavailable.

Talismanic winger Rafael Leão has been ruled out of the fixture after picking up a fresh muscle injury during a training session.

He joins American forward Christian Pulisic on the sidelines, who is still nursing a severe bone bruise sustained during the summer World Cup, while defender Matteo Gabbia failed to travel following a late ankle knock.

In a dramatic tactical move, Amorim has also completely frozen Christopher Nkunku, Youssouf Fofana, David Odogu, and Fikayo Tomori out of the travelling roster due to ongoing squad exclusions.

On a positive note, veteran midfielder Luka Modrić has returned to full fitness and is heavily tipped to start in central midfield to anchor a depleted Milan lineup.

Manchester United enter their final pre-season fixture showing relatively stable form under Michael Carrick, recording two wins, two draws, and one defeat. The Red Devils bounced back from an early 1-0 defeat to Wrexham by thrashing Rosenborg 5-0 and beating Atlético Madrid 2-1. Successive 1-1 stalemates followed against Paris Saint-Germain and Leeds United, though they defeated the latter 5-4 on penalties to claim the BoyleSports Cup.

AC Milan have endured a frustrating, winless pre-season campaign as new manager Rúben Amorim struggles to establish his system amid a severe squad crisis. The Rossoneri opened their summer schedule with back-to-back scoring draws, finishing 2-2 against Celtic before playing out a tense 1-1 derby stalemate with Inter Milan. However, their form slumped heavily in their last outing, suffering a comprehensive 3-0 defeat to Chelsea in Jakarta.

AC Milan: Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlovic; Chukwueze, Modric, Comotto, Estupinan; Loftus-Cheek, Ramos, Saelemaekers

title: Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen – Match preview and team news
description: Newcastle will play the German Side Bayer Leverkusen at their home ground on Saturday in another pre-season friendly match before the Premier League kicks off next week.Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen ...
fullText:
Newcastle will play the German Side Bayer Leverkusen at their home ground on Saturday in another pre-season friendly match before the Premier League kicks off next week.

Venue: St. James' Park, Newcastle.

Newcastle United head into their next pre-season fixture under new manager Matthias Jaissle with a mix of injury boosts and setbacks.

The Magpies are managing the return of Fabian Schär and Lewis Miley, who are both nearing full fitness following groin and fibula injuries and could feature for limited minutes today.

However, Tino Livramento remains sidelined with a severe calf and knee ligament injury, undergoing rehabilitation in the United States and ruling him out of the upcoming Premier League opener.

Left-back Lewis Hall is a late fitness doubt due to a minor knock, leaving Dylan Charlton on standby to start.

In attack, summer signing Bazoumana Touré is expected to start on the left wing, while Anthony Elanga has recovered from a recent injury scare to occupy the right flank.

This fixture serves as a crucial integration period following the high-profile summer departures of Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimarães.

Bayer Leverkusen approach this Tyneside friendly adjusting to life under new head coach Carles Martínez Novell while balancing several squad absences.

Midfielder Robert Andrich will miss the trip to England entirely; despite scans clearing him of serious structural damage after an injury against Sevilla, he remains on an isolated individual training program.

Youngster Montrell Culbreath is also ruled out following a knock in that same Sevilla fixture, and forward Eliesse Ben Seghir remains unavailable due to a lingering hamstring issue.

On a positive note, Nathan Tella and Axel Tape have returned to full training and are available for selection after missing recent pre-season matches.

Key figures Victor Boniface and Aleix García, who started on the bench during the recent friendly defeat against Nottingham Forest, are expected to feature heavily at St James' Park to build vital match sharpness ahead of the new Bundesliga campaign.

Newcastle United have endured an inconsistent pre-season campaign, resulting in a 40% win rate over their last five games. The Magpies secured victories against Darlington (3-0) and Valencia (2-1), but struggled with structural changes under Matthias Jaissle. They suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat to Bristol City and enter today's fixture fresh off a disappointing 3-1 loss against Everton, highlighting defensive vulnerabilities and finishing inefficiencies.

Bayer Leverkusen have shown stellar summer form, winning five of their six pre-season matches while racking up 19 goals. Under Carles Martínez Novell, they dominated opponents with victories over Sevilla (2-1) and Rot-Weiss Essen (3-0). Their perfect run was only recently snapped on Wednesday by a narrow 2-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest, where Patrik Schick continued his hot streak by scoring his fourth goal in three games.

title: Kahleah Copper’s next honor cements her place among Rutgers’ greats
description: PHOENIX — Kahleah Copper’s basketball journey from Rutgers to the Phoenix Mercury is about to add another milestone. Copper will officially take her place in the Rutgers Athletics Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class.
fullText:
PHOENIX — Kahleah Copper's basketball journey from Rutgers to the Phoenix Mercury is about to add another milestone.

Copper will officially take her place in the Rutgers Athletics Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class. The honor is a reminder of where one of the Mercury's biggest stars began.

The guard finished her Rutgers career with 1,872 points, ranking third on the program's all-time scoring list. She led the Scarlet Knights in scoring in each of her final three seasons and was a two-time Second Team All-Big Ten selection.

Mar 9, 2014; Uncasville, CT, USA; Rutgers Scarlet Knights guard Kahleah Copper (2) shoots against Connecticut Huskies forward Breanna Stewart (30) during the second half in the semifinal round of the American League Athletic Conference Tournament at Mohegan Sun Arena. UConn defeated Rutgers 83-57. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-USA TODAY Sports

The guard also helped Rutgers win the 2014 WNIT championship and was named tournament MVP. Those accomplishments helped establish the foundation for what Copper would eventually become in the WNBA.

Copper would find success in Chicago with the Sky, winning a championship and the 2021 WNBA Finals MVP.

Then came her arrival in the Valley.

Mar 9, 2014; Uncasville, CT, USA; Rutgers Scarlet Knights guard Kahleah Copper (2) looks for an opening against the Connecticut Huskies during the second half in the semifinal round of the American League Athletic Conference Tournament at Mohegan Sun Arena. UConn defeated Rutgers 83-57. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-USA TODAY Sports

The Mercury acquired Copper in February 2024, making her a centerpiece of the franchise's future. In her first season with the Mercury, Copper averaged a career-high 21.1 points per game, finished third in the league in scoring and earned her first All-WNBA honor. She also won Olympic gold with Team USA that summer.

Since arriving in Phoenix, Copper has continued to establish herself as one of the faces of the Mercury. Her scoring, toughness and competitive edge have made her a key part of the team's identity, while her experience as a champion has given Phoenix a proven leader to build around.

Jul 17, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Phoenix Mercury guard Kahleah Copper (2) against the Connecticut Sun at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

Now, Copper's Rutgers legacy is officially being cemented, while her story in Phoenix continues to be written.

The induction will take place on Oct. 2 at Jersey Mike's Arena, with the class recognized Oct. 3 when Rutgers football hosts Indiana.

title: Stella Hemetsberger Finishes Natalia Diachkova To Retain Muay Thai World Title In ONE Fight Night 46 Main Event
description: The two-sport queen successfully defended her gold with a knockout performance in U.S. primetime!
fullText:
Two-sport queen Stella "Always Hungry" Hemetsberger made a statement in her first ONE Women's Strawweight Muay Thai World Title defense, stopping Natalia "Karelian Lynx" Diachkova via knockout in the third round of the main event at ONE Fight Night 46, which aired live in U.S. primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, August 14.

Both women played it cautious to open the contest, feeling each other out until Diachkova exploded into a boxing combination that got the defending World Champion's attention. Hemetsberger answered with kicks, but the Russian superstar caught one of them and dumped her to the canvas to close the frame.

Hemetsberger came out of her shell in round two, firing right hands at the challenger, who was looking to overthrow her.

Diachkova answered right back with punches of her own, though the 27-year-old Austrian neutralized the exchanges by clinching up whenever "Karelian Lynx" threatened to find her range.

All caution went out the window in the third stanza. A more confident and accurate Hemetsberger came out swinging, driving a left kick into Diachkova's liver, which clearly hurt her.

Diachkova hunched over in pain, and then the two-sport queen delivered the same kick to the same spot moments later.

As the 31-year-old Russian turned away toward the ropes, Hemetsberger closed the show with a three-punch combination and a knee that forced the referee to step in and wave off the contest at the 1:46 mark.

The dominant finish saw Hemetsberger, who also holds the ONE Women's Strawweight Kickboxing World Title, further cement her status as one of the top pound-for-pound female strikers on the planet. She also moved her professional record to 11-1 and earned a US$50,000 bonus for her extraordinary performance.

title: Sean Payton Goes Viral With Shot at Falcons Fans During Broncos’ Preseason Opener
description: He still has his edge. The post Sean Payton Goes Viral With Shot at Falcons Fans During Broncos’ Preseason Opener appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Before patrolling the sidelines for the Denver Broncos, Sean Payton did it for the New Orleans Saints, and old habits formed during that time have not died.

Payton has faced the Falcons 31 times as a head coach, and his teams have won 22 of those contests. His Saints faced the Dirty Birds twice a year for 15 seasons as the two teams battled for the NFC South crown.

The rivalry got a fitting renewal from Payton in the preseason opener.

GettySean Payton dropped strong words about the Falcons as the Broncos cruised to victory.

Payton drew attention as the Broncos headed into halftime with a sizeable lead on the Falcons for his comments to Cynthia Frelund.

"A lot of people dressed up as empty seats today," Payton told Frelund at the break.

"#Broncos Sean Payton can't resist taking shot at #Falcons during his halftime interview on @9NEWSSports," The Denver Post's Troy Renck posted on X in reaction. "Not going to lie. I think it is hilarious."

#Broncos Sean Payton can’t resist taking shot at #Falcons during his halftime interview on @9NEWSSports. Notgoing to lie. I think it is hilarious. pic.twitter.com/xiEX7aREuV

— Troy Renck (@TroyRenck) August 15, 2026

"Sean Payton has lost none of the petty when it comes to Atlanta," The Denver Post's Parker Gabriel posted.

"Sean Payton (still) has no love for the #Falcons," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport posted.

Payton's remarks, which were over a quarter-million views in 90 minutes, were not lost on the Falcons' base, either. One appeared to concur with the Broncos' head coach's assessment of the scene inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium amid his team's blowout victory in the preseason opener.

"Dang shots fired by Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton," WSBTV's Alison Mastrangelo posted, noting the halftime remarks.

The fan absolved Payton of blame for the comments.

A fan account posted, "You can't blame him," in the replies to Renck's post, adding, "You have to put a team on the field that he can't make fun of and that people want to spend their money to go see."

GettyThe Broncos have some items to clean up.

The Broncos carried a 24-0 lead into halftime. And while they surrendered a touchdown in the third quarter and missed some field goals, there is another issue that Payton and the Broncos coaching staff are expected to address.

"Broncos have to be pleased with SO much of this game," DNVR Broncos' Zac Stevens posted on X, adding, "But Sean Payton will NOT be pleased with the penalties. And he shouldn't be.

"Can't have this like they did last year. HAS to get cleaned up."

Stevens noted that the Broncos had eight penalties before the third quarter ended. They carried that into the 2-minute warning. Still, after finishing with the fourth-most penalties during the 2025 regular season, it is indeed an issue. Payton and the Broncos coaches will likely address it.

Payton and the Broncos tacked on another win against the Falcons to his record. It does not count, and they will not face one another in the regular season.

You would not know that listening to Payton, though.

The Broncos expect to have many more outcomes like their eventual 27-7 preseason-opening win over the Falcons during the regular season. They have some items to address, but it was an encouraging start for Payton and the Broncos.

title: It was a night of firsts for Wellen Park, including a first football win
description: The Eagles made their athletic debut on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, and it was a winner as Wellen Park beat North Port in its first football game.
fullText:
NORTH PORT – It was a night of firsts for a brand new high school, yet sophomore Curtis Bowdre's first was one he'd rather forget.

He was the first Wellen Park player to touch a football in a game. He muffed the punt.

But everything that Bowdre and his Wellen Park teammates did after that first-quarter miscue – including an 87-yard touchdown return by the 5-foot-7 speedster on the second-half kickoff – pointed to a surprisingly game-ready roster as the Eagles pulled away for a 45-7 preseason victory over new rival North Port on Friday, Aug. 14.

First, some more firsts: Jason and Nichole Wireman, proud parents of sophomore quarterback Noah Wireman, were the first fans in line when the gates opened almost two hours before game time. Jacob Hyer, a 22-year-old senior at the University of West Florida and son of head coach Sascha Hyer, sang the National Anthem.

There were "Inaugural Game" T-shirts and shiny game programs with lots of advertising. A bell in the end zone rings every time one of the local heroes does something worth celebrating. Decorative posters lined a fence, honoring 13 seniors in the "Class of 2026" (oops), and there was even a pre-game helicopter flyover. When Eagles kicker Donovan Childers finally put boot to ball at 7:31 p.m., a football program was born.

Bowdre's fumbled punt came after North Port went three-and-out on the game's opening possession, and a nervous Wellen Park offense did little when it got its first chance. Instead, Cameron Wilson's 13-yard TD pass to Zachary Patchell – four plays after his 42-yard hookup with senior Caleb Lawrence – staked the visiting Bobcats to a 7-0 lead with 4:32 left in the first quarter.

"I had to get it back," said the 150-pound Venice transfer. "I had to make up for what I did in the first half."

He reached the end zone again on an apparent 46-yard TD pass from Wireman (7-of-14, 191 yards, 1 TD) midway through the third quarter, but a teammate's block in the back at the 4-yard line negated the points. Will Campbell's 4-yard run two plays later, however, made it 45-7 anyway and triggered a running clock.

"Honestly, I wasn't expecting this," Hyer said. "You work for it, but when you're dealing with 15-to-17-year-olds, you don't know what's going to transpire. That first quarter, I was thinking, 'Wow, we're in a dogfight.'"

Once settled in, Wellen Park scored five touchdowns and a field goal on six drives, including an 11-play, 59-yard march to answer Patchell's early TD. Wireman scrambled 8 yards and Childers kicked the first of six extra points for a 7-7 tie.

"I came ready and focused," Wireman said. "I don't worry about a crowd. I worry about what's on the field, that's it. You could feel the momentum shift during the second quarter."

Campbell's 3-yard run on the second snap of the second quarter after a North Port fumble inside its own 5 gave the Eagles a lead that would last the rest of the night. He scored three times and carried 14 times for 73 yards, as Wellen Park churned to a 336-236 advantage in total offense.

"This is only one game," Hyer said. "Obviously, I know that North Port has struggled a little bit. I get that. Our schedule is set up to where we can compete. Did I expect this? No. But a competitive game, that's what I was looking for."

Doors were opened and classes began just four days earlier.

North Port has only one winning season (6-4 in 2023) to show for 22 years of football, and is coming off a 1-9 effort last fall. Obviously, three turnovers and a staggering 24 penalties for 180 yards didn't help.

"We walked into a game with a really good atmosphere and we made some mistakes," Bobcats coach Devon Gales said. "We're playing a preseason game. We're looking to expose things as a team that we need to fix, and I think we're going to have a lot of film to watch this weekend."

Penalties, penalties, penalties. Those 24 flags for 180 yards will give Gales a lot to talk about. "That's going to happen in a preseason game, the first game of the year," he said. "Those are the things that you fix."

There is some loyalty to be found in these Bobcats. Unlike so many North Port teams of the past, several key members of last season's group are back, including sophomore quarterback Wilson (6-of-18, 159 yards, 1 TD, 1 int) and senior running back Ayden Guerra (six carries, 28 yards). "We preach to our players to be who you say you are," Gales said. "And these are players who are loyal to our school and loyal to their community and stayed. We don't want anybody other than those who want to be here."

The clock is ticking before the real season begins. The Bobcats' regular-season opener is a Thursday home matchup with IMG Academy State. "We do have an older team, so six days isn't that big a deal," Gales said. "We just have to sit down and look at the mistakes. We get another chance to play football on Thursday."

Establishing the run became a second-half priority. After managing just 54 yards on 17 first-half runs (including four carries for 26 yards by Wireman), the Eagles stressed the ground game after Bowdre's kickoff return made it 31-7 – adding 91 yards on 14 tries during a 13-minute span. "We had runs, but there were maybe miscommunications with the running back or they bounced it out, they weren't patient enough," Hyer said. "I told the (offensive coordinator), 'Keep running, it's going to bust. Just be patient. It'll be there.'"

Another first was Hyer's first pre-game speech. Asked what he told his team before the historic kickoff, the Eagles' 53-year-old head coach said he urged them "to have that chip on your shoulder. You guys are the kids that nobody wanted. … It's not really true, but I tried to dig into them a little bit. A little anger. A little hatred. We're not supposed to be here."

The "Venice Effect" is strong. About 35 players at all levels in the Eagles' program came from long-time powerhouse Venice, in addition to the half-dozen assistant coaches. Hyer had 47 players in uniform for the preseason game, but that Venice core – including Wireman and Bowdre – will be a season-long theme. "Realistically, when I look at our program, one kid from Venice (defensive tackle Collin Gilkerson) actually had varsity time," Hyer said. "But they've all been playing together."

title: Brewers can’t rally in ninth again, lose to Dodgers, 3-1
description: The offense had another rough night, managing just one run, five hits, and four walks
fullText:
For the second straight night, the Brewers fell behind and needed a late rally. They loaded the bases in the ninth, but couldn't break through this time and lost to the Dodgers, 3-1.

Early on, the Brewers made Yoshinobu Yamamoto work. Even though they only managed one baserunner — a Jake Bauers walk — in the inning, Yamamoto needed 26 pitches to get through it. Meanwhile, Robert Gasser was efficient for the Brewers, needing just 14 pitches for the first inning. However, the Dodgers hit three singles in that inning, the last of those a Mookie Betts single to drive in a run. That put the Brewers down 1-0 after one inning.

From there, the two starters matched each other with scoreless innings in the next three frames. The Brewers had a scoring chance in the third after Joey Ortiz hit a one-out double, but he was left stranded there after Garrett Mitchell and Jackson Chourio both struck out. The Dodgers had a scoring chance with two outs in the bottom of the inning after Andy Pages singled and stole second, but he was stranded there.

The Brewers' offense broke through in the fifth inning. Luis Lara led off the inning with a long double that just barely stayed in the park. It did set up the offense. David Hamilton went for the bunt, and it was a good one that went for a single. Ortiz brought in the run after that, hitting a sharp line drive but right at Kyle Tucker. It was more than deep enough to score Lara, and the Brewers tied the game at 1-1.

Unfortunately, that was all the offense could manage that inning. Mitchell struck out again, and Chourio grounded out to end the inning.

That tie didn't last long. In the bottom of the inning, Andy Pages hit a two-out solo home run to left field, and the Brewers were down again, 2-1. One inning later, Tommy Edman added another solo home run to center, extending the deficit to 3-1.

Gasser pitched into the seventh, starting the inning by getting a line out from Hunter Feducia. After walking Shohei Ohtani, his day came to an end. It was a solid day for Gasser overall. He allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings, allowing eight hits and one walk while striking out seven. It was also the most pitches he has thrown in a game, as he finished the day with 102 pitches thrown.

Meanwhile, Yamamoto mostly kept the Brewers in check, but the Brewers managed to get him out of the game after six innings. He allowed just one run, four hits, and two walks, and struck out nine Brewers.

The bullpens kept both offenses in check for the next two innings. Evan Phillips and Tanner Scott pitched scoreless seventh and eighth innings for the Dodgers. Grant Anderson finished out the seventh inning scoreless and worked around a walk. Bryse Wilson pitched the eighth inning and struck out the side.

Once again, the Dodgers brought in Edwin Díaz to close in the ninth inning. It started out looking like it could be a repeat of last night. Andrew Vaughn led off the inning and worked a full count before getting hit by a pitch. He was replaced by pinch-runner Jihwan Bae, who stole second on a 1-1 count. It put a runner in scoring position, but Christian Yelich struck out for the first out of the inning.

William Contreras was up next, and Díaz was struggling heavily as he threw five pitches all out of the strike zone, walking Contreras. His first pitch to Lara was high and inside as well, then he threw a slider right down the middle. Lara hit it sharply on the ground, but Edman made a running grab to rob Lara of a base hit. It wasn't quick enough to turn a double play, so Edman took the sure out of Lara at first.

That moved both baserunners up to second and third, putting the tying run in scoring position. Hamilton was up next, and Díaz continued to struggle to throw strikes. Hamilton didn't swing once and drew a five-pitch walk. Ortiz was up next with another chance with the bases loaded. Unfortunately, he couldn't complete the rally for the Brewers, grounding out to Betts to end the game.

The offense remained subdued again, managing just one run, five hits, and four walks. Those hits were scattered among five different Brewers, with Bauers and Hamilton the only two Brewers on base twice. They had their scoring opportunities tonight, but went 1-for-6 with runners in scoring position and left eight on base.

With the series tied 1-1, the Brewers will send their ace to the mound tomorrow night. Jacob Misiorowski will face Justin Wrobleski in Saturday's game, which will be a national broadcast on FOX. First pitch is at 6:15 p.m.

title: Paul Finebaum Blasts Commanders’ Jayden Daniels Over LSU Rift
description: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is at odds with the LSU Tigers football program after the school gave his former No. 5 jersey to sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett. Daniels wore No. 5 during his time with the Tigers and became the program’s third Heisman Trophy winner in 2023.As a result, Daniels’ attorney sent a cease-and-desist […] The post Paul Finebaum Blasts Commanders’ Jayden Daniels Over LSU Rift appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is at odds with the LSU Tigers football program after the school gave his former No. 5 jersey to sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett. Daniels wore No. 5 during his time with the Tigers and became the program's third Heisman Trophy winner in 2023.

As a result, Daniels' attorney sent a cease-and-desist letter, a copy of which ESPN obtained, to LSU athletic director Verge Ausberry on Aug. 5, telling the school it could no longer use Daniels' name, image or likeness.

Amid the Commanders star's rift with LSU, Paul Finebaum of ESPN didn't hold back his thoughts on the situation and put Daniels on blast.

"I got to know Jayden Daniels when he was at LSU," Finebaum said during an Aug. 14 appearance on The Team 980. "I really liked him and talked to him a lot. I would interview Brian Kelly. Even when he went to the Commanders, there was a great sense of pride in what he did the first year.

"I said all that to say this: He's lost all of that from everywhere and everyone in LSU Nation after what happened this week [and] I know it's been said here before, but I rarely have ever seen a dumber, more senseless move.

"I don't know who pulled the strings, but all the cleanup on aisle three from Jayden Daniels from this moment on will not be enough. He has made a terrible mistake. He can be successful in Washington. I hope he is. But I would advise him to never waste another second in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, because they are done with him."

Moreover, Finebaum went into further detail on how the LSU crowd would receive the Commanders QB should he decide to head down to Baton Rouge to watch a Tigers game this 2026 college football season.

"I think it would be chillier than Inauguration Day at the nation's capital," Finebaum added about the reception that Daniels would receive from the crowd. "I think it's one thing if there was a misunderstanding, but when the report came out yesterday about the cease and desist and giving the trophy back, that's just pure stupidity.

"There are plenty of copies of the Heisman Trophy. I don't think anybody knows which one is the original because every school has one in its trophy case. Every player has one at home."

On Aug. 13, Joe Burrow, LSU's second Heisman Trophy winner, received a question after the Cincinnati Bengals' 16-14 preseason win over the Detroit Lions.

"I don't know too much about it," Burrow told reporters postgame. "I just heard about it a couple hours ago [and] I don't necessarily have too many thoughts at this time; I just don't know enough about the situation to have any thoughts, I would say."

Furthermore, Burrow spoke about whether LSU ever intends to hand out his No. 9 jersey, given that it is the issue Daniels is having with the football program.

"Like, they haven't," Burrow added. "Yeah, they told me that they wouldn't use it again, but you never know what happens."

title: Edwin Diaz Captures Shaky Save vs. Brewers to Even Up NLCS Rematch
description: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not waver in his support for Edwin Diaz, and the skipper was rewarded.
fullText:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not waver in his support for Edwin Diaz, and the skipper was rewarded.

The Dodgers beat the Brewers 3-1 on Friday, August 14th, in a game where they battled offensively and on the mound, but still ground out another tough win.

The Dodgers close the gap to the Milwaukee Brewers, back down to one game, putting them in the running for the top speed in the National League.

In the top of the ninth inning, just like last night, the trumpets blared, and it was Edwin Diaz's second straight save chance.

Diaz hit the first batter he faced on a 3-2 count, and the Brewers put in a pinch runner, who stole second base shortly after.

Luckily, Christian Yelich struck out for the first out, and then Diaz walked William Contreras. Things were looking shaky away with the winning run at the plate, but thanks to Tommy Edman, Diaz got a clutch out at first base.

Diaz needed an open base as he walked David Hamilton after, loading the bases and making every fan hold their breath with two outs.

Edwin Diaz, after the game, on Dave Roberts and the Dodgers' support: 

"It means a lot to me. I'm in a rough stretch right now, but I keep working hard and trying to make pitches," Diaz said.

"Today it wasn't easy, but I got the job done, so I'm happy."…

Dave Roberts did not look nervy at all, and he kept Diaz in to figure things out. He produced a weak grounder to short for the third and final out, picking up his seventh save of the season.

For Dodgers fans, it likely did not inspire much confidence, but for Diaz, it must have been a weight off his shoulders and, at least for now, a sigh of relief.

Yamamoto produced a ho-hum six-inning outing with just one run allowed, two walks, and nine strikeouts.

The Japanese ace showed better stuff and more aggressiveness than expected.

He was really trying to get some swing-and-miss, though the approach led to a lot of pitches early on, as can happen; he got efficient as time went on and produced a good outing in terms of length.

Still, it was more than good enough to set up the bullpen for success. Evan Phillips and Tanner Scott were lights out after, allowing the team to win on the mound.

Hitting-wise, Andy Pages led the way with a standout 3-for-4 game, along with Tommy Edan getting his swing in check again, going 2-for-4.

Overall, it is a signature modern Dodgers win, and it is something to feel good about heading into Saturday's third game against the Brewers, this time facing the Cy Young favorite in Jacob Misiorowski.

The Dodgers will hope Justin Wrobleski is able to bounce back after a run of rough outings.

title: Purce and Kerr score in Gotham's 2-1 comeback over the Kansas City Current
description: Midge Purce and Sam Kerr scored goals to give Gotham FC a 2-1 comeback win over the Kansas City Current on Friday night.  In other action around the National Women's Soccer League, the San Diego Wave and the Denver Summit played to a 1-1 draw; the Utah Royals beat Bay FC 3-2; and the Seattle Reign topped the Chicago Stars 1-0.
fullText:
Midge Purce and Sam Kerr scored goals to give Gotham FC a 2-1 comeback win over the Kansas City Current on Friday night.

In other action around the National Women's Soccer League, the San Diego Wave and the Denver Summit played to a 1-1 draw; the Utah Royals beat Bay FC 3-2; and the Seattle Reign topped the Chicago Stars 1-0.

Amelia White scored for the Current (9-8-3) just 22 seconds into the match to tie an NWSL record. Croix Bethune earned her league-leading ninth assist on the goal, which ended Gotham's shutout streak at 307 minutes over three matches.

Purce tied it in the 13th minute and Sam Kerr scored in the 41st minute to put Gotham (13-3-4) in front at Sports Illustrated Stadium and stretch the team's unbeaten streak to eight games.

Current defender Elizabeth Ball was shown a red card for a foul on Gotham forward Jordynn Dudley in the 27th minute after a corner kick but after a video review it was downgraded to a yellow card.

Kansas City's Vanessa DiBernardo made her first start since returning from maternity leave.

Yazmeen Ryan's second-half goal pulled the Summit (6-7-6) into a draw in San Diego.

Melanie Barcenas opened the scoring in the 35th minute with a left-footed shot from distance for the Wave (10-7-3).

Denver captain Janine Sonis' cross into the box found Ryan who headed it home to pull the Summit even in the 58th minute.

Summit defender Eva Gaetino was subbed off due to injury in the 16th minute.

Utah's Miyabi Moriya, Narumi Miura and Mina Tanaka made NWSL history as three Japanese players scored in the same match for the first time in the Royals' win over Bay FC.

Karlie Lema's pressure gave Bay FC (5-10-4) a lead in the sixth minute, but Moriya responded a minute later to tie it and Utah (11-6-3) took the lead in the 22nd minute on Narumi's shot from outside the box.

Bay defender Heather Gilchrist headed home her first professional goal to equalize.

Tanaka scored on a penalty shot in the 79th minute to give Utah the win.

Bay FC's newest acquisition, defender Jenna Nighswonger, made her debut as a sub in the 62nd minute.

Maddie Mercado scored on a rebound in the 53rd minute to lead the Reign (8-7-3) past the Stars in Seattle.

Goalkeeper Claudia Dickey made two saves for her fifth clean sheet of the season.

After parting ways with head coach Marin Sjögren and assistant coach Anders Jacobson, Karina Báez made her debut as interim coach for Chicago.

The Stars (4-14-1) are winless in their last six games.

title: Young starlets power Ontario past Ashland in season opener
description: Three of the Warriors' four goals came from a freshman and sophomore.
fullText:
ONTARIO - Coach Larry Atkinson and his staff wondered where the goals would come from this fall.

"That was our big question," he said. "We had everybody back on defense — plus a girl that hasn't played the last couple years back — so we knew we'd be solid there.

"Where are we going to get the shots from? Where are we going to get some goals from?"

ARROWS RUN RAMPANT! Ashland boys soccer routs Ontario in emphatic season opening win

It took just 30 seconds for Ontario to record its first shot on goal Friday evening and less than nine minutes to put the ball in the back of the net for the first time in the Warriors' 4-2 win over Ashland.

"I think we came out really strong," freshman Keatyn Kilgore said. "We have some stuff to work on because it's the beginning of the season, but I feel like we came out strong and put it together. But we have a lot to work on still."

There is a lot to work on, sure. But there's a lot to be impressed with already with Kilgore netting a brace, senior Braelyn Llewellyn and sophomore Mia Moton also joined in on the scoring, and Maia Fox had an assist.

"We had a chance to score a goal in the first 30 seconds ... and I think we had 20 shots on goal, which is a lot," Atkinson said. "We have to get more efficient, but the field was sloppy and that hurt us because we have speed. We like to move the ball and it just wore them out because you're stepping into something deep, you're going down in the ground, it's hard on your legs, but we persevered and got through it.

"Then every time we scored, they would come back. We finally got the two-goal lead and kept that ... we made a goalie mistake and we can't have that, can't give anybody a free goal. But overall, for our first game after the summer we've had, I'm very pleased."

Llewellyn opened the scoring in the 9th minute before Kilgore doubled the advantage in the 26th. Just before the half, though, Ashland junior Mia Gonzalez pulled one back tapping in a cross from senior Aliviah Sauder. Moton finished off a counterattack four minutes into the second half to restore the two-goal lead before Gonzalez struck again two minutes later. Kilgore latched onto a through ball from Fox in the 58th minute as a buffer goal, and the Warriors would then lean on defense to close out the win.

"We could have had a lot more goals, we just need to work on some stuff and our finishing," Kilgore said.

"We missed some shots we should have made, but we'll chalk it up to nerves for the first game or the conditions," Atkinson added. "We have a week to get ready for Lexington and see what we need to work on."

For the Arrows, there's a lot coach Lee Hunt wants to work on after the first match.

"We started a little slower than I wanted to," he said. "There were some bright spots in the game at times ... we'll go back to work this week before we play again Thursday."

Gonzalez's brace was the highlight for Ashland and flashes of the team's potential were on display.

"There's a lot of could have on this team, there's a lot of reasons to be excited for what this team can do throughout the season," Hunt said. "It's a long season and this is just game one."

title: Grantsville rallies from 12-point deficit, scores 30 unanswered to stun San Juan 30-20
description: For the first quarter and a half against Grantsville Friday, it looked like San Juan was going to remind everyone why it was one of the most dangerous offensive teams in Utah.  Then Grantsville’s defense took over.  The Cowboys erased a 12-0 deficit by scoring 30 unanswered points, forcing seven San Juan turnovers along the way, and held on for a 30-20 victory at Snow College.
fullText:
For the first quarter and a half against Grantsville Friday, it looked like San Juan was going to remind everyone why it was one of the most dangerous offensive teams in Utah.

Then Grantsville's defense took over.

The Cowboys erased a 12-0 deficit by scoring 30 unanswered points, forcing seven San Juan turnovers along the way, and held on for a 30-20 victory at Snow College.

It was a game that seemed to change every few minutes. San Juan came out firing as quarterback Beau Yeomans opened the scoring with a 1-yard touchdown run, and later in the first quarter he found Brigg Palmer wide open for a 47-yard touchdown.

Just like that, San Juan had a 12-0 lead.

And then the Broncos stopped scoring, although it took a while for the Cowboys offense to get going as they threw two interceptions deep in San Juan territory.

But Grantsville's defense kept giving the offense another chance.

"We left a lot of points on the board," Grantsville coach David Millward said. "We had interceptions in the end zone. I think we had four red-zone possessions without points."

Eventually, though, the Cowboys broke through when Carter Bell scored on a 9-yard run early in the second quarter, cutting San Juan's lead to 12-7.

Then late in the first half, Mack Hammond intercepted Yeomans and gave Grantsville the ball at its own 42. Crew Allred immediately ripped off a 34-yard run, and then with 2.4 seconds left before halftime, Allred rolled to his left and found Ty Holm for a 24-yard touchdown.

Suddenly, the team that had trailed 12-0 was leading 13-12.

The Cowboys opened the second half by forcing another San Juan turnover when Palmer fumbled at the San Juan 30.

Grantsville turned that opportunity into another touchdown, with Bell punching it in from the goal line. A successful two-point conversion pushed the lead to 21-12.

Bell added another touchdown later in the quarter, this one on a 7-yard toss play, and Cache Hammond's 37-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter made it 30-12.

That was 30 straight points for Grantsville.

San Juan finally showed some life again late in the fourth when Yeomans found Palmer for a 39-yard touchdown with 5:25 remaining and Randall Black ran in the two-point conversion to make it 30-20.

The Broncos got one more chance when they forced Grantsville to punt, but after driving deep into Cowboys territory, Yeomans threw another interception to Graeson Warren.

That was Warren's second interception of the night and effectively ended San Juan's final serious threat.

For Millward, the biggest thing wasn't that his team played a perfect game. It absolutely didn't. It was that the Cowboys kept fighting anyway.

"I'm just so proud of our kids," Millward said. "They just battled and battled, and we made a lot of mistakes, but they just kept believing."

Grantsville's defense did more than just create turnovers. It swarmed San Juan throughout the night.

"They just swarm and swarm," Millward said. "That's what we like to say, that we just play hard-nosed football in Grantsville, and I feel like tonight, that's what we did."

And that's probably the best way to describe the game. San Juan looked like the better team early, then Grantsville made play after play.

For a Grantsville team that spent much of the first half leaving points on the field, its defense made sure it would get enough chances to eventually make them count.

And when the Cowboys finally did, they didn't stop.

title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Faces Backlash for Mistake During Blue Jays Series
description: The New York Yankees lost their series opener against the Toronto Blue Jays, 3-1, on Friday night.It was another inconsistent performance from Jazz Chisholm Jr., who recorded one hit in four at-bats and is now 5-for-his-last-35 at the plate.Chisholm Jr.’s Base Running MistakeOne moment that stood out during the game came when Chisholm Jr.
fullText:
The New York Yankees lost their series opener against the Toronto Blue Jays, 3-1, on Friday night.

It was another inconsistent performance from Jazz Chisholm Jr., who recorded one hit in four at-bats and is now 5-for-his-last-35 at the plate.

One moment that stood out during the game came when Chisholm Jr. lost track of the number of outs in the inning.

With two outs, Chisholm Jr. watched the ball in the air after a Yankees hitter made contact. The Blue Jays eventually caught it to end the inning, but Chisholm Jr. reacted extremely late and nearly found himself in a costly situation.

This also isn't the first time this season that Chisholm Jr. has lost track of the outs while on the base paths.

Jazz Chisholm forgot the number of outs again. pic.twitter.com/PXVvxZZ4m9

— Dan Clark (@DanClarkSports) August 15, 2026

As expected, Yankees fans who have already criticized Chisholm Jr.'s play this season didn't react lightly to the former All-Star's mental mistake.

"Wow…how do they continue to put up with that," a fan said.

Someone else added, "Some players you watch daily and just respect. Some players you watch daily and lose respect. Jazz is a player you have to watch daily to really get it."

Another person wrote, "The only way you fix this is by pulling him from the game and benching his [explicit] for the weekend."

"He needs to be benched," a fan shared.

One more fan commented, "Tired of his act."

It's been a tough year for Chisholm Jr., and he'd be the first one to tell you that. He's discussed his struggles on several occasions this season.

"If I knew, I would already have fixed the problem," Chisholm said about his play. "Even when I think I'm getting going hitting, it's still an out. I'm still hitting it right at someone. I can hit it 107 (mph) and still hit it right at someone."

He's currently batting .216 across 394 at-bats with 85 hits, 17 home runs, 48 RBIs and 31 stolen bases.

title: Brett Hull Raves About Ex-Maple Leafs Captain Wendel Clark’s Legendary Toughness
description: Brett Hull raved about Maple Leafs legend Wendel Clark's toughness, praising his skill set and ability to take on the toughest enforcers. The post Brett Hull Raves About Ex-Maple Leafs Captain Wendel Clark’s Legendary Toughness appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Brett Hull raved about former Toronto Maple Leafs captain Wendel Clark for his legendary toughness. Hull highlighted Clark's well-rounded skill set and ability to fight the toughest enforcers in the league.

Clark, 59, was selected 1st overall by the Maple Leafs in the 1985 NHL Draft. Despite being drafted as a defenseman, the Kelvington, Saskatchewan, native became a left-winger when he entered the NHL.

Clark's tenacity was on full display, as he would do anything possible to help his team win. Whether it was scoring a goal, throwing a big hit, or fighting to shift momentum, Clark was crucial to Toronto's success.

Hull, 62, witnessed Clark's impact firsthand while playing for the St. Louis Blues. The Blues and Leafs played in the Norris Division. Players have hilariously referred to it as the Chuck Norris Division because of the number of enforcers on each team.

Brett Hull heaped praise on Wendel Clark for his toughness on and off the ice. The two-time Stanley Cup champion recalled that the Leafs legend even getting the better of legendary enforcer Bob Probert.

"Will you guys agree with me that Wendel Clark is one of the greatest hockey players ever?" Hull posed to Sheldon Souray and Russ Courtnall on an episode of his Ice Guardians Podcast. "You wanna go on YouTube and everyone says Bob Probert. Wendel Clark used to beat the [expletive] out of Bob Probert. Clark is the toughest human being on the planet."

Hull also pointed to Clark never being afraid to sacrifice his body to land a big hit. He said that his style of play and effectiveness on the ice ultimately separated him from the rest.

"Dude, he was a killer. When he hit [Bell] behind the net with the Blues. It is absolutely crazy," Hull said.

Russ Courtnall also chimed in and shared Hull's sentiments about Clark's legendary toughness. Both players were teammates on the Leafs, and were among the team's core players.

Courtnall recalled one game in particular in which Clark fought Bob Probert, who is widely considered the toughest NHL enforcer. He said the former Leafs captain not only did well against Probert, but also issued a warning to Basil McRae.

"We have a 5-on-5 brawl in Detroit. I'm playing for the Leafs and Wendel is beating the [expletive] out of Bob Probert. And every time he's punching him, he's looking over," Courtnall told Ice Guardians Podcast. "Basil [McRae] is just lifting me up and choking me. And Wendel starts telling Basil, as he's beating Probert up, 'If you don't let him go, you're next' and Basil let me go. That's how tough Wendel is. He was unbelievable."

Courtnall also emphasized how tough Clark was during his career.

"[Clark was] drafted as a defenseman, never played one shift in the NHL as a [defenseman]. And, he scored goals and beat the crap out of every player. Toughest guy. Thank God he was my teammate," Courtnall said."

title: Transfer shocker? Bayer Leverkusen could be eyeing blockbuster sale
description: Is the former FC Bayern star leaving Leverkusen?
fullText:
According to a report from Sky Germany journalist Florian Plettenberg, Bayer Leverkusen could be contemplating a sale of attacking midfielder and former Bayern Munich academy prospect Malik Tillman — if it can receive a financial windfall for the USMNT star:

🚨🆕 Bayer 04 Leverkusen are open to selling Malik Tillman for an exceptional offer.

The 24 y/o attacking midfielder is now one to watch until Deadline Day.

Speaking to Sport Bild (via BuLiNews), Tillman said he wants to understand Martínez's plan before deciding what comes next, noting that the transfer window remains open.

Tillman was particularly candid about his first season at Leverkusen, describing the 2025/26 campaign as the "worst" of his career. The 24-year-old acknowledged that he failed to reach the level expected of him, but also suggested that his relationship with former coach Kasper Hjulmand contributed to his struggles.

Leverkusen invested €35 million to sign Tillman from PSV Eindhoven, creating significant expectations. Tillman recognizes that price tag and believes he must prove his value on the pitch. At the same time, he feels he lacked important support last season, specifically mentioning a lack of trust from his coach and backing from the club.

With a new coach now in charge, Tillman appears ready to wait and see whether his situation improves before making a final decision on his future.

title: Primetime Friday matches open soccer seasons for RV, Marion Harding
description: River Valley went to Harding Stadium to face the Presidents in a Futbol Friday Night soccer doubleheader season opener Aug. 14.
fullText:
MARION — Soccer season is officially underway in Ohio, and Marion Harding and River Valley took advantage of Futbol Friday Night.

The OHSAA starts the boys and girls soccer seasons a week ahead of the high school football, giving those athletes the chance to compete in prime time Friday, Aug. 14.

The Marion County and Mid Ohio Athletic Conference rivals faced off in a girls-boys doubleheader inside Harding Stadium with the RV girls prevailing 5-1 over the Presidents and the RV and Harding boys playing to a 1-1 tie.

Here's more from Futbol Friday Night 2026:

There was little to quibble about for the Vikings. The defense was on point. The midfield helped control the tempo. The offense got contributions from all over the field.

"This sets the tone for the season a lot of times in what you're going to be," RV coach Justin Hage said. "It's a big rivalry so you're anxious and up and crazy from the beginning. You get that win and it helps you with the rest of the season to push a little harder. We have some games coming up that are rough, and we have to get ready for those."

River Valley received its first goal from Chloe Addis with 27:22 left in the first half, then less than 10 minutes later Sarina Strother struck. Kya Moran made it 3-0 late in the first half as the Vikings took the three-goal lead into the second half.

The Vikes struck again less than seven minutes after halftime when Cassidy Elliott scored. Strother then hit a rocket from deep with 15:20 left to give her team a 5-0 lead.

"Our defense I thought looked really, really good. There were times in the preseason where they didn't look that sharp, but I think they took care of each other," Hage said, giving credit to goalkeeper Havyn Rodgers for her aggressiveness and communication in the net. "Our passes connected really well. It's a little better when we're on grass. We took a lot of shots from a lot of different people. Four people scored."

Vote in the soccer polls: Marion Star Boys, Girls Preseason Soccer Player of the 2026 polls

Soccer video: Marion-area soccer teams optimistic about the start of 2026 season

With 67 seconds to go, the Presidents got a goal from Charlee Etgen in front of the net.

"It's a positive at the end of the game to score a goal and get the first goal of the season out of the way. Hopefully we'll feel more confident going into our next game," first-year Harding girls coach Kindall Duke said.

It's a young crew at Harding in 2026 as they lost 11 to graduation so their inexperience was evident at times.

"We have a solid core group of girls. We just need a little bit more communication and more leadership," Duke said.

The Presidents led most of the night, dominating possession and taking 15 shots at River Valley goalkeeper Cooper Mullins. It was a Harrison Keith ricochet less than four minutes into the match that gave Harding a 1-0 lead.

"In the beginning I was challenging our guys, and I wasn't reacting to what was going on," RV coach Joel Richards said. "It's on me. I don't call it a fluke goal. I call it a good goal because they were pressing and doing what their coach wants them to do and that's why that goal went in. It was purely on effort on their end. They outplayed us from the beginning."

Largely a group of juniors, Harding showed its overall improvement as a soccer team from the previous two seasons during its match with the Vikings.

"Taking over the program two years ago and coming off back-to-back 1-win seasons, it's taken time," Harding coach Ian Hartley said. "The biggest thing now is taking the opportunity and learning how to win matches. Just because you are the dominant team doesn't mean you always come out on top."

With 17:05 left in the match, Gideon Owings found Riley Hummel on a breakaway that evened the match at 1-1. Two minutes later, a skirmish broke out and yellow cards were given to players on both teams with RV going a man down for the final 15 minutes. Harding continued to pressure to score but couldn't crack RV's defense.

"Our emotions were very high," Hartley said. "We stayed composed for the most part when it got kind of sketchy there for a minute. We need those (leaders) to step up in big moments. We just weren't quite there tonight, but hopefully we can get there."

Richards liked his team's defensive effort and obviously the play of Mullins, but there are things to learn from as the Vikings get ready for a busy next week with three road matches lined up at Johnstown, Buckeye Valley and West Jefferson.

"Ian had a great game plan. They absorbed a lot of our stuff and sent it back up the field. It frustrated us," Richards said.

This article originally appeared on Marion Star: Primetime Friday matches open soccer seasons for RV, Marion Harding

title: ‘Levels to this’ – WNBA fans hype up Caitlin Clark after dominant display against Paige Bueckers
description: Caitlin Clark got one over Paige Bueckers after the Indiana Fever beat the Dallas Wings on Friday night. Her fans on social media were quick to hype up the superstar.
fullText:
Caitlin Clark got one over Paige Bueckers after the Indiana Fever beat the Dallas Wings on Friday night. Her fans on social media were quick to hype up the superstar.

Caitlin Clark put in a superstar display as the Indiana Fever beat the Dallas Wings 98-87 on Friday. The 24-year-old had 29 points and 10 assists in the game.

Ever since she got drafted, Paige Bueckers has been propped up as a potential rival for Clark to be considered the face of the WNBA in the future. So this was a statement victory for the Fever star.

Bueckers had 29 points herself, but it wasn't enough to make the difference. And after the game, social media was abuzz with praise for the Iowa alum.

Clark has an incredibly passionate fanbase, as one of the most popular athletes in the United States. This season, those fans are enjoying plenty of opportunities to crow.

The 3-time All-Star controlled the offensive side of the game from start to finish. It was an important win in the race for seeding ahead of the playoffs, too. Unsurprisingly, this earned her a lot of praise online.

"I love Paige too, but CC just showed here there are levels to this game," one fan commented. "Yeah, I've seen enough. Caitlin is going to be the GOAT," another added.

"CC deserves 10 more assists. She was just ridiculous," a comment said. "CC has been on a tear and put on a clinic. Dallas had no chance," a fourth fan wrote.

"Anyone can see Caitlin Clark has multiple MVPs written all over her," claimed a different fan. "CC outplayed Paige and IMPOSED HER WILL on the Wings," observed a sixth fan.

Clark's historic night also included just one turnover, it was as complete a performance as could be. There is no denying that she deserves all the flowers after this dominant display.

title: Tate edges Pine Forest 17-14 in kickoff classic, takeaways
description: Tate and Pine Forest went back-and-forth in Friday's kickoff classic. Here's what to know from the Aggies 17-14 win.
fullText:
As Tate was marching down the field for a game-winning drive late in the final minutes against Pine Forest in both teams' kickoff classic, Aggies head coach Rhett Summerford asked senior kicker Ethan Priest about his range.

Priest, who just started learning the position last year, said he was good from anywhere inside the 40-yard line. Fortunately for Tate, the Aggies drive started at the Pine Forest 35-yard line, and Priest nailed a 21-yard field goal as time expired to give Tate a 17-14 win.

In just over a year of kicking, Priest has hit three game-winning field goals, with the first two coming against Booker T. Washington and Escambia in the 2025 regular season.

"I knew that he was going to make that chip shot," Summerford said of Priest. "When the pressure's on, he usually makes the kick."

Priest's kick ended a kickoff classic where both varsity teams played the second half. The freshman teams played the first quarter, while the JV teams played the second quarter.

Tate senior running back Ethan Pittman's 11-yard touchdown was the lone score in the third quarter before the flood gates opened in the final frame. Pine Forest quarterback Jacorie Thomas cut the Aggies lead to 7-6 with a seven-yard touchdown run on the first play of the second quarter, then Pittman answered with a seven-yard touchdown to put the Aggies in front 14-6.

Pine Forest answered to tie the game 14-14 as Thomas ran for a nine-yard touchdown then found Tulane commit Korden Randle for the two-point conversion.

Here's what else to know from the scrimmage.

It wasn't just Priest's kick that made the difference. Both teams had their ups and downs on special teams.

Priest missed his first extra point of the night, but Tate was called for a false start and he converted after Pine Forest accepted the penalty to move back the kick five yards. Summerford wanted to see Priest punt better too, though one of his short punts in the fourth quarter was muffed by Pine Forest muffed the punt and recovered by Joseph Soho to set up the Aggies second touchdown.

The Eagles also allowed two long kickoff returns and were called for a personal foul on the last one, setting up a short field for Tate's game-winning drive. Pine Forest also missed an extra point in the third quarter.

"I like the fact that we were courageous enough to go for the return on a bad kick," Pine Forest head coach Kerry McDowell said. "If he picks it up, there was no one in front of him for the next 70 yards. He muffed the ball and that was the difference in the game, a turnover down in their red zone and that's what gave them the win."

The two teams were supposed to play in a kickoff classic last year, but it was cancelled due to weather.

This year's matchup gave both defenses the test they needed after replacing a lot of talent from stingy units in 2025.

For the Eagles, they faced a run heavy Aggies squad with a big offensive line led by FIU commit Darell Villanueva, a good challenge for a defense that returns one starter in the front seven from a year ago. Tate marched down the field easily on the opening drive, but Jeremiah Bolden intercepted a pass on the next drive. The Aggies grinded out their last two drives as Pine Forest tired from playing a lot of snaps.

It only gets tougher for Pine Forest next week against a Booker T. Washington squad that may have the best offensive skill position talent in the Pensacola area.

"With Washington's ability, golly, you just try to slow them down," McDowell said. "They've had so many kids move in it's going to be hard to defend them all."

Tate's defense got to match up against a veteran Pine Forest offense with plenty of speed. Senior quarterback Jacorie Thomas was decisive in both the running and passing game, while senior wide receiver and Tulane commit Korden Randle and junior three-star tight end Kemarion Jordan showed why they'll be playing on Saturdays with big catch-and-runs.

"They're huge," Summerford. "(Jordan), I was just hoping someone would tackle him. Then they got speed at quarterback, which is really, really tough. But I'll tell you this, we needed a test for the jamboree. Missed out on it last year and I was really proud that we got it in this year. We're a little battle tested now."

With junior running back Tanner Clark not dressing for the scrimmage, the senior running back got over carry for the Aggies tonight, racking up over 100 yards and two touchdowns.

Pittman followed his blocks all night, then showed some shiftiness on his two touchdowns run. Clark will be back next week when Tate opens its season against Marianna, creating quite a 1-2 punch for opponents to handle.

The pair combined to run for 2,268 yards and 23 touchdowns a year ago and now are a whole year older and stronger.

"We got two of them and I think they're both very special," Summerford said.

This article originally appeared on Pensacola News Journal: Tate edges Pine Forest 17-14 in kickoff classic, takeaways

title: William Osula turns 23 and says he is looking forward to the new season under a new boss
description: William Osula has a huge season ahead of him. After injury issues and struggling for form, a late run of starts towards the end of last season saw the young striker given the chance to get into a groove and he started to look the part.
fullText:
William Osula has a huge season ahead of him.

After injury issues and struggling for form, a late run of starts towards the end of last season saw the young striker given the chance to get into a groove and he started to look the part.

Five goals in his final seven Premier League matches of the 2025/26 season suggested a real quality player could be emerging.

Nine goals in total in domestic competitions last season despite starting only 11 matches, real hope for the future.

That late season club form helped William Osula get his first senior start for Denmark.

The Danish striker turned 23 earlier this month and now he has the platform to make more huge strides this season.

However, he will be doing it without the manager who brought him to Newcastle United.

Jason Tindall had done some coaching at Sheffield United back in the day, before he and Eddie Howe came to St James' Park in November 2021. On Tindall's recommendation of the raw talent he'd seen when William Osula was very young in the Blades set-up, Eddie Howe agreed to buy the inexperienced striker for £10m (plus a potential £5m in future add-ons) in summer 2024.

Eddie Howe and Jason Tindall have now moved on and William Osula has now been interviewed by BBC Newcastle: "There are some things that you don't expect but I spoke to them and wished them all the best for the future. I showed my gratitude for all they've done for me and how they have helped me so far."

Matthias Jaissle is the new man and William Osula says that the NUFC squad are "all excited" about taking on the upcoming season under Eddie Howe's replacement.

The Denmark international commenting: "We have got a new manager and I'm looking forward to working with and playing well under him. A new manager bringing in a new style that he likes to play, so everyone is getting ready for the season to start next week."

It has been a hectic summer and a significant transformation on and off the pitch.

William Osula adding: "We have already learned his playing styles in and out of possession and how he likes to play tactically. It has been good. I want to continue to show what I can do, remain confident. I know what I can do on the pitch so it's just keeping doing that."

title: Are fans now more invested in star names than clubs?
description: From Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo to Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham, are star names a bigger draw than club for young fans?
fullText:
The golden ticket came gift-wrapped in flamingo pink. Instantly iconic. Nailed on to adorn bedroom walls from Buenos Aires to Barcelona and be splashed across billboards the world over.

Lionel Messi's arrival at Inter Miami was about as sure a marketing hit as you could ask for. Social media accounts spiked, shirts sold out, match tickets went for stupid money.

But new followers hadn't just come for the Herons.

"A lot of people are walking around cities and towns in the UK and Europe wearing that flamingo pink of Inter Miami with zero affiliation to Miami, having never been there," explains sports brand strategist James Kirkham.

"It's quite a normal thing now. But it is the player who has done the job."

That football lovers should want to show a connection with arguably the greatest player of all time comes as no surprise - likewise his long-term rival in the now-distinct yellow of Al-Nassr.

Messi or Cristiano Ronaldo. Barcelona or Real Madrid. MLS or Saudi Pro League.

These generational superstars have long stirred heated debate, from curious kids with jumpers for goalposts to social media cultists armed with memes and virtual binders of blistering stats.

But this trend of following individual players transcends merely Messi and Ronaldo.

"It's been happening for a while, ever since the sheer impact and influence of gaming, particularly on young fans," says Kirkham, who remembers a swell of support for Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

Kirkham says younger fans are actually "less rigid or tribal than they used to be" and boast a "more encyclopaedic knowledge" developed through video games - including EA Sports FC or Football Manager. Other touch points come via YouTube and trading cards.

They follow teams from different countries or leagues not for the badge on the front, but because of the name on the back.

"Fans play as these players in games," says Kirkham. "So there is a really thin line between virtual and real life.

"Following a player and buying them as part of your Ultimate Team and then wearing that player's name on the back of your shirt, be that Atletico Madrid or Chelsea or Dortmund, kind of makes no difference."

To paraphrase Eric Cantona, you can change most things in life but never your football team.

Who you support is primarily an emotional connection forged through family or geography. In many cases, you're born into it.

According to a study called 'The Rise of the Second Club Fan', however, published before this summer's World Cup, 80% of global supporters now also follow a second team.

Head of insights Matthew Kyle, who authored the report by Engage and MTM, says that does not mean fans are abandoning the team they have supported their whole life, rather choosing another or sometimes multiple others to engage with too.

It can be more common in countries or regions that do not boast a strong league, with geography no barrier to second-club fandom.

"They are often looking for 'who else can I support?' It's more natural," adds Kyle.

This can be a more rational choice - fans might relate to the club's story, their culture and values, or simply like their kit.

The most powerful entry point to following a second club the study suggests, though, is players - meaning support can move when the player does.

"For this audience, they are the club," adds the report. "These fans track individuals, not institutions."

It was the summer of 2018, days before France kicked off their World Cup-winning campaign that Antoine Griezmann laid out his plans for the big reveal.

'The Decision', he teased, would come at the end of a half-hour documentary broadcast on Spanish TV. Barcelona thought they had him, as did most fans when Gerard Pique - whose company produced the show - tweeted a popcorn emoji.

At the end of the documentary, however, Griezmann stood in front of the Metropolitano and revealed he was staying at Atletico Madrid in one of two different endings reportedly filmed to keep the decision secret.

The self-confessed NBA fanatic - inspired by LeBron James' live show by the same name in 2010, when the basketball star joined the Miami Heat - was attempting to own his narrative. Instead he, and Pique, caught some criticism.

Kyle says that "self-commercialisation" did not have the impact it would have done now if it was Erling Haaland or Kylian Mbappe.

Griezmann was almost before his time. Many prominent players now share regular updates from their lives on their own YouTube channels - from Haaland, to Ronaldo, Jude Bellingham and Lionesses' star Ella Toone.

"Players are becoming their own distribution levers, with some in particular taking a driving seat in terms of 'how I project myself onto the world' and building their own channels and audience," explains Kyle.

Now, in many cases, the players do own the narrative and fans are increasingly able to invest in their journeys, which are more accessible than ever.

"Players are far more culturally symbolic than they used to be," says Kirkham. "It is not that players don't do endorsements now, but they know they have to resonate with fans, so fans can really latch on to them and get behind them.

"Look at what Marcus Rashford did during Covid in terms of changing actual legislation.

"Young fans want to know players stand for something more - that gives them more chance to follow and pursue them, find a deeper connection with them.

"They look for stuff that is aligned to them, who they are, their causes and where they're from. I think we will increasingly see that."

With eyes around the globe focused on North America this summer, the World Cup was a great launch pad for many players' personal brands.

Vozinha, the previously little-known Cape Verde goalkeeper, became a cult hero for his heroics against Spain - the 40-year-old's Instagram growing from 50,000 to nearly 30 million followers.

But big-name players were also big winners. Spain and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal saw a huge spike in followers, as did Bellingham. Even Ronaldo, the most-followed athlete on Instagram, experienced a healthy leap.

Most notable, though, was Norway forward Haaland, whose popularity skyrocketed as fans flocked to his Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat accounts.

Haaland's winning formula was a mix of his humble and relatable persona - whether sporting a cowboy hat or helping Norway's kit man - a very active social media presence in which he comments and replies to posts, and being the centre of viral clips and memes, from his "bromance" with former team-mate Bellingham to the Russian model who shared an uncanny likeness to the forward.

"Haaland was a massive winner from the World Cup," says Kyle. "He gained more than 51 million followers since 1 July on his social accounts - bear in mind the first six months of this year he only gained 11 million.

"Oviously he had a good World Cup. But a massive part of it was the personality coming across, interacting with fans, memes, his stature and what he looks like, Norway being there [in the last eight] for the first time and the fans' rowing celebration - all that kind of stuff."

Indeed, Haaland has almost 20 million more Instagram followers than his club Manchester City and, as mentioned, his own YouTube channel.

"You'll see more and more creating their own entertainment formats, content networks, and that is away from the clubs," adds Kirkham, who worked with Harry Kane on the England captain's app Cleats Club, aimed at helping the forward reply to fans' questions on his own terms.

"The clubs are very aware, but they can't do a lot other than build their own club ecosystem. It is difficult because they don't fully own the player - they can go and talk about their favourite rap music on a show or do a podcast.

"It will be a continual trade off, where the club get everything from them because of shirt sales but they know ultimately they are human with their own power to do the shows and content they want."

It is, however, good news for fans, says Kirkham.

"It means more and more for them," he adds. "Fans have an insatiable appetite for football and the chances are it can't be fully quenched, because at the moment you can't put enough out there.

"Whatever the platform you're choosing to pursue players on, there is more and more for you as a fan. Players and fans are realising that and leaning into it increasingly."

The question for clubs is whether they can keep those fans who arrived because of a player when they leave.

That brings us on to another theme - the national hero.

Turkish side Trabzonspor are currently experiencing such a windfall after signing Egypt star Mohammed Salah following his glorious nine years at Liverpool, while Tottenham Hotspur enjoyed a decade of Son Heung-min before the South Korea icon joined LAFC last summer.

"Son is a great example," says Kyle. "He wasn't a global superstar when he arrived but he was a huge player from South Korea, and over the course of his time with them Spurs became the most-supported foreign club there, topping Manchester United.

"Now, when Son left, Spurs didn't immediately lose millions of followers on their socials from Korea. But we did see a small spike on his new club."

Kyle says it is about trying to deliver content those fans still want to engage with.

"The easy answer is to say global superstars will do it on their own and these clubs without them will struggle," he adds. "But every club has characters.

"Every player leaves eventually, even if they leave by retiring at your club. So it's about using them as an asset while there and thinking about how all fans are also interested in stuff off the pitch.

"Behind the scenes content always does really well. Even if you're not a fan of that club, you might stop scrolling and watch 'a day in the life' of a player because it might be good content."

Think Welcome to Wrexham. Which poses another thought: perhaps we're entering the era of fans following the star owner, too?

"Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac would have been a huge draw for people who don't know football," adds Kyle. "On the counter, there will be people in the football community saying 'this will be interesting because what the hell do they know?'.

"You've got the benefit of football being like soap opera - seasons of television, seasons of football, different stories. And football never ends."
