title: Mired in nasty slump, Brewers don't believe time off needed for William Contreras
description: William Contreras dropped to 0 for his last 20 with another tough night at the plate, but Pat Murphy says he wants to keep playing him
fullText:
LOS ANGELES – Pat Murphy issued a homework assignment to the dozen or so assembled reporters huddled around his desk at Dodger Stadium the afternoon of Aug. 14.

"I'd like you guys to figure out how many balls William [Contreras] has hit on a line to right-center, to center, to right field at 100+ this year for an out," he said.

Murphy's query was in response to a question about the slumping catcher's inclusion in the lineup after yet another bad night at the plate. Contreras was 0 for his last 17 entering the day and was coming off a game with a pair of unsightly at-bats that ended by striking out.

Contreras did also hit a ball hard and in the air, lining out at 104 mph to center field at one point, and that swing stuck with his manager.

"That changes your perspective a little bit," Murphy said.

Shortly thereafter, the answer to Murphy's question was presented: Seventeen, the most on the Brewers and 24th-most in baseball.

That sentiment is one of the reasons Murphy has continued to play Contreras just about every day in spite of a prolonged funk that has seen his OPS dip more than 100 points from .810 in late June to .702 now.

Contreras entered the game Aug. 14 slashing .163/.248/.264 since the calendar turned to July. In the second half, he was batting .159.

His hitless streak ran to 20 at-bats with an 0-for-3 showing – though he did have an 18th 100+ mph air out to center or right and walked in a ninth inning rally that fell short – and he's also 4 for his last 43.

"William's an all-star man," Murphy said. "He'll be just fine."

The skipper's inquiry prompted a follow-up: Just how unlucky, exactly, has Contreras been?

Translation: Contreras may be a bit unlucky this year, but that's not the primary reason he's struggling.

The biggest reason why Murphy keeps trotting Contreras out there while Gary Sánchez is one of the hottest hitters on the team?

He doesn't think that, with the way Contreras is wired, a day off is going to be of service.

"I don't think William is going to get out of it by simply sitting on the bench," Murphy said. "It might be something I try if it doesn't work. But when he gets three ground ball hits between the 5-6 hole, that doesn't mean he's back, either."

Contreras, renowned around the team for his desire to play every day, himself expressed that the way out of the hole was to keep on swinging.

"Keep going," he said earlier in the week. "Keep doing what I do. Keep working harder."

So far on the road trip, the slumps of the Brewers two highest-paid hitters, Contreras and Christian Yelich, haven't broken. Contreras 0 for 15 while Yelich is 2 for 14 with a homer.

"We have a lot of guys going through it," Yelich said. "No one feels sorry for you. You just got to keep going and keep working. That's the only way it gets better. If you stop doing that then it's definitely not going to get better. You got to keep working and try to find something that sticks."

Yelich can at least point to some rough sledding in the luck department, with a 96 mph lineout Aug. 14 following three hard-hit outs the preceding day. One of those outs was a 101 mph flyout to left field that seemed ticketed for the seats before dying at the warning track.

"It's hard," Yelich said. "It's a results based game, right? You can only trust the process for so long. Eventually you have to start having things go right and producing. Hopefully that's around the corner. I don't know what else to do beside keep working.

For better or worse, Yelich and Contreras are the Brewers' guys. If they soar, it will likely be on their backs. If they sink, it will be at least in part be on their batted balls straight down into the ground.

Yelich hopes better results are around the corner. Murphy believes that's true. He and the Brewers have no other choice.

This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Mired in nasty slump, Brewers don't believe time off needed for William Contreras

title: Real Madrid midfield ace could make surprise appearance in starting XI against Schalke despite earlier doubts
description: A lone Brahim Diaz goal helped Real Madrid to a narrow 1-0 win over Deportivo de A Coruña earlier this week, and the club now stare at their final pre-season clash ahead of the new campaign.The game ...
fullText:
A lone Brahim Diaz goal helped Real Madrid to a narrow 1-0 win over Deportivo de A Coruña earlier this week, and the club now stare at their final pre-season clash ahead of the new campaign.

The game will be played against Schalke tomorrow evening, and it will be a critical game for Jose Mourinho and Co. as it will mark the return of several recently returned international stars and even new signings.

With the manager planning several tactical tweaks, especially in midfield, it will be a great opportunity for Mourinho to test out various combinations.

Bellingham's return to training is massive on that front, but the player's participation tomorrow was said to be in doubt.

Now, as reported by COPE, Bellingham has arrived in very good physical condition, and there is not much he is lacking in terms of match fitness.

Bellingham could start tomorrow. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

If he completes the training session today normally, there is even a possibility that the World Cup semi-finalist starts against Schalke tomorrow.

Also expected to start on the night are the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Yan Diomande and Thibaut Courtois, and the upcoming game may be the closest Real Madrid XI to the one that will start on match day 1.

With Diomande's arrival, it is clear that Mourinho will count on a 4-3-3 setup for the upcoming season, and there is no question of compromising the attack to add an extra body in midfield.

The middle of the park, however, was exactly where Real Madrid struggled last season, both to create chances and to control the game, and Mourinho has a big puzzle to solve on that front.

Mourinho has big decisions to take in midfield. (Photo courtesy: Real Madrid official website)

Word has it that the manager sees Bernardo Silva as a non-negotiable starter, likely in deep midfield alongside Aurelien Tchouameni.

Jude Bellingham, as matters stand, is the overwhelming favourite to start in the attacking midfield.

Such a setup, however, leaves no place for Federico Valverde or Arda Guler, who are critical to add physicality and creativity, respectively. Moreover, there is also a report that the manager sees Trent Alexander-Arnold as an option for the midfield.

There is not much time left for the manager to put his ideas into practice, and tomorrow's game will be critical on that front.

title: Mbappé: “We are going to win titles”
description: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé talked to Real Madrid TV and previewed the upcoming season shortly after rejoining the squad in training. “I am very happy to be back and to have my first impressions with the team, with the new staff, with all the teammates, and with the people here in Valdebebas. It’s always […]
fullText:
Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé talked to Real Madrid TV and previewed the upcoming season shortly after rejoining the squad in training.

"I am very happy to be back and to have my first impressions with the team, with the new staff, with all the teammates, and with the people here in Valdebebas. It's always good to come back here to play and to prepare for the season," said the attacker.

This will be the first time Mbappé works under José Mourinho.

"We talked a lot during the World Cup, and he has spoken with me extensively. I arrived a few days ago, and I think it's very positive to have a coach like him, someone who knows how to win and how to guide us towards victory. I think every player is delighted to have a coach who knows where he's going, and that's positive for us," he explained.

Mbappé is confident that the team can turn things around.

"We have to win. I am sure that this year we are going to win titles again. That's what we want, and that's what's going to happen. I feel that the team is eager, and we are going to stay focused all year to bring joy to all the madridistas. There is nothing more important than winning titles with the team, feeling the joy, and giving that joy to the fans," he concluded.

title: Barcelona ‘absolutely convinced’ two blockbuster transfers will happen this summer
description: Barcelona remain fully committed to signing Rodri and Julian Alvarez, with the Catalan giants convinced that both transfer operations can be completed before the summer window closes.According to Mund...
fullText:
Barcelona remain fully committed to signing Rodri and Julian Alvarez, with the Catalan giants convinced that both transfer operations can be completed before the summer window closes.

According to Mundo Deportivo, there are no doubts within Barcelona over their plans for the final weeks of the market.

With just over two weeks remaining, the club is not actively looking at alternative targets for either position.

The Rodri to Barcelona transfer is currently the more advanced of the two situations, while the pursuit of Julian Alvarez remains more difficult because of Atletico Madrid's position.

Still, Barcelona believe that the wishes of both players could prove decisive as they look to deliver two major additions for Hansi Flick's squad.

Barcelona's confidence over the signing of Rodri is largely based on the player's desire to join Flick's project.

Barcelona are in advanced talks to sign Rodri. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

The Spanish midfielder has returned to Manchester City following his summer break, but Barcelona remain convinced that he wants to make the move.

The financial side of the operation still needs work, as Barcelona are aware that their second offer must be improved, with Manchester City demanding a package worth around €80 million.

The Catalan club, however, are not believed to be willing to meet that figure outright.

They plan to increase the overall value of the proposal through bonuses and add-ons, potentially taking the package closer to €70 million.

Notably, City have rejected Barcelona's previous approaches and are waiting for an improved offer, although the player's future remains uncertain.

According to Mundo Deportivo's report, Barcelona expect the Rodri transfer to be wrapped up no later than next week.

Julian Alvarez is pushing for a move to Barcelona. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

The situation surrounding Julian Alvarez to Barcelona is more complicated.

Atletico Madrid have maintained a tough stance over the Argentine striker, making the operation far more difficult than the negotiations for Rodri.

But Barcelona remain confident that the player has not abandoned his hope of joining the Blaugrana.

Alvarez is expected to continue pushing for an exit over the coming days, with the 26-year-old still focused on finding a route from Atletico to Camp Nou.

His attempt to involve Diego Simeone in facilitating his departure has not yielded the result he wanted, but that has not changed his desire to play for Barcelona.

Simply put, the player's power is now central to Barcelona's hopes. Atletico's position may remain firm, but the club is betting that Alvarez's continued determination could eventually change the course of the negotiations.

title: Roads to close for Tour of Britain Women
description: The cycling race will set off through Cumbria on Wednesday.
fullText:
The Lloyds Tour of Britain Women gets under way on Wednesday, with roads closing to allow the cycling race to pass through.

The opening stage will start and finish in Cockermouth, Cumbria, and take riders on a 158.9km (99 mile) route through communities across west and north Cumberland.

The race route will pass through places including Whitehaven, Workington, Maryport, Allonby, Silloth, Abbeytown, Wigton, Caldbeck and Aspatria, with rolling road closures expected from about 10:40 to 16:30 BST.

Further stages in the five-day race will go through Blackpool, Llandudno and Hay‑on‑Wye before finishing in Leamington Spa on 23 August.

Cumberland Council said most roads on the route would be subject to rolling closures, meaning traffic would be temporarily held for short periods as the riders and race convoy passed through.

Wednesday's race is expected to pass through at the following times:

High Harrington: 11:57 to 12:07

Lead vehicles may arrive about 15 minutes before the riders.

Road closures in Cockermouth will also accommodate the start and finish areas.

Main Street and Station Street will be closed from 04:00 to 18:30, while South Street will be closed from 07:00 to 17:00.

Crown Street, Sullart Street and Gallowbarrow would be closed between 09:00 and 11:30 to allow event infrastructure to be installed safely, the council said.

In addition, the A595 between Bothel and Cockermouth will be closed from around 14:00 to 15:35 while riders completed the final sections of the stage.

title: Is he Germany's next Urbig? 18-year-old already looks world-class
description: When your performance in your first professional game is immediately described by your teammates as “world-class,” you must have done a lot right. At just 18 years old, Florian Hellstern is alread...
fullText:
When your performance in your first professional game is immediately described by your teammates as "world-class," you must have done a lot right. At just 18 years old, Florian Hellstern is already the starting goalkeeper for SpVgg Greuther Fürth. And that at a club many experts had already tipped as a relegation candidate before the season.

Key attacking players such as Noel Futkeu and Branimir Hrgota have left, so others now have to step up. In goal, that means Hellstern, who was loaned from VfB Stuttgart. At first glance, the move may seem risky for the young goalkeeper, but if the youngster takes off, he could reignite the battle for places at his parent club in Stuttgart in a whole new way.

Hellstern already showed in the 1-1 draw against St. Pauli that he has enormous quality and was not called "probably Germany's most exciting goalkeeping talent" at his unveiling for nothing.

After the final whistle, the praise for the German youth international kept coming, because with several saves he rescued a point for his team. "I've rarely seen someone so young bring that much calmness and self-confidence. He gives us tremendous security. And at 18 years old, that's crazy. You shouldn't praise too much, but that was a very good game today," captain Florian Klaus told 'Bayrischer Rundfunk'.

📸 Selim Sudheimer - 2026 Getty Images

His coach Heiko Vogel was also full of praise: "The boy is truly gifted. My job is to keep him at the right altitude."

So the move to Fürth may not have been risky after all. The fact that it can also prove to be a masterstroke was already shown by two of his predecessors. Just two years ago, Jonas Urbig played for the Cloverleaf, and now he is considered Manuel Neuer's successor at Bayern. Jürgen Klopp is also likely to have him on his radar for the German national team. Nahuel Noll also used Fürth as a springboard. He could start the new season as SC Paderborn's number one if he beats out Markus Schubert.

These examples likely helped Hellstern decide in favor of the Cloverleaf. Now, in the coming weeks, he has to prove that his performance against St. Pauli was not a one-off. At the same time, the goalkeeper must be careful not to get carried away by all the praise. But his coach is optimistic: "The personality that is already there will only grow even more. The boy has to stay healthy and keep a clear head. But I have no worries about that at all. The boy is brilliant."

Hellstern himself also said at his unveiling that he is "really excited" about this challenge and now wants to prove himself at a higher level. In Fürth, he has the opportunity to develop further both as a player and as a person.

If things go as well for him as they did for Urbig, Stuttgart's battle for places could be reignited in a whole new way next year. Dennis Seimen, who is also only 20, is currently injured and is not expected to feature for VfB until after the international break in mid-October. Depending on how he performs in the Bundesliga, Hellstern could be the next competitor waiting in the wings next summer.

So while Hellstern's performances could cause Seimen concern in the future, VfB itself can at least look ahead to a bright goalkeeping future. No other Bundesliga club is likely to have two such talented young goalkeepers with enormous potential in its squad.

title: High school football roundup for Friday, Aug. 14 (Week 1)
description: High school football roundup for Friday, Aug. 14 (Week 1)
fullText:
Layton Christian (1-0) dominated Hunter (0-1) in a nonregion matchup, scoring 48 unanswered points before the game ended after three quarters under the UHSAA 44-point mercy rule. The Eagles jumped out to a 28-0 lead in the first quarter. Quarterback Colton Johns threw four touchdown passes, and Chris Munroe scored twice on the ground.

Grady Anderson orchestrated a dominant performance for Kanab (1-0), leading them to a convincing 47-13 victory over Emery in a nonregion matchup. Anderson threw four touchdown passes, including a spectacular 69-yard connection with Brennan Orton late in the first quarter to set the tone. Emery (0-1) struggled to keep pace despite a brief spark in the second quarter when Ajay Thomas rushed for a 2-yard touchdown, cutting the deficit to 20-13. Kanab's Lochlon Glover broke free for a 41-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter, extending their lead and dashing any hopes of an Emery comeback. With this win, Kanab's balanced attack on both air and ground showcased their strength as they held Emery scoreless in the second half.

Desert Hills (1-0) dominated Hillcrest in a nonregion matchup, shutting out the Huskies 40-0. The Thunder scored all 40 points in the first half, with quarterback Deacon Virgin throwing three touchdown passes in the second quarter alone. Virgin connected with Josiah Thomas, Tagg Brinton and Isaac Andresen for a 26-yard score with 1:21 remaining in the half. Desert Hills' defense held Hillcrest scoreless throughout the game.

Canyon View (1-0) dominated Jordan in a nonregion matchup, shutting out the Beetdiggers 35-0. The Falcons scored touchdowns in all four quarters, with Owen Williams connecting on multiple passing touchdowns and Jace Floyd adding two rushing scores.

Rich (1-0) defeated Gunnison Valley (0-1) 21-14 in a nonregion game. The Rebels built a 14-7 lead through two quarters, with Nash Parry catching a 7-yard touchdown pass and Max Weston adding a 28-yard touchdown reception. Gunnison Valley scored on a Kyle Keith's 2-yard run in the second quarter, then pulled within seven again with Brody Knudsen's 80-yard pass reception with 5:48 remaining in the fourth.

Salem Hills (1-0) dominated Granger (0-1) in a nonregion matchup, with Joe Hughes accounting for three touchdowns in the rout. Hughes caught a 3-yard touchdown pass and a 36-yard touchdown pass from Cash Hollingshead while also breaking free for a 69-yard scoring run in the third quarter. Salem Hills scored on its first possession when Lindon Woodland returned an interception 34 yards for a touchdown, setting the tone for the SkyHawks' 41-7 victory. The Lancers' only score came on a 3-yard run by Maa'imoa Havili with 2:00 remaining in the fourth quarter.

Lehi (1-0) cruised to a 35-13 victory over Maple Mountain (0-1) in a nonregion game, highlighted by standout performances from Cam Wren and Sam Verbecky. Wren caught a 74-yard touchdown pass from Briggs Jensen just three minutes into the game, setting the tone for the Pioneers. Verbecky added to the offensive onslaught with a 67-yard touchdown run shortly after, helping Lehi build a 21-6 lead by the end of the first quarter. Wren also secured a 21-yard touchdown pass from Jensen in the third quarter, further extending Lehi's dominance. Maple Mountain's Mason Robinson found the end zone with a late 3-yard touchdown reception from Joey Imperial in the final quarter, but it was not enough to close the gap.

Green Canyon defeated Provo 10-6 in a defensive struggle Friday night. The Wolves scored first when Ethan Munk connected with Huston Paremski on a 27-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. Provo answered with a 4-yard touchdown run by Teave Brown in the third quarter, but Green Canyon sealed the victory with a 34-yard field goal by Boston Daines with 4:49 remaining in the fourth quarter.

Eli Braegger recorded four touchdown receptions as Bear River (1-0) defeated Ogden 36-13 in a nonregion matchup. In the Bears' first game under new coach Craig Anhder, Braegger caught an 18-yard pass from Preston Wilkinson with 2:53 left in the fourth to cap his standout night. Wilkinson connected with Braegger for earlier scores of 54, 49, and 10 yards as Bear River pulled away in the second half. Ogden (-1) managed to score back-to-back touchdowns in the third quarter, highlighted by a 2-yard run from Ryker Rice, but couldn't keep up with Bear River's explosive offense. The Bears' defense held Ogden scoreless in the first, second, and final quarters.

Justice Taylor shone in his first outing under new head coach Mike Cole, leading Payson (1-0) to a narrow 20-19 victory over Mountain View (0-1) in a nonregion game. Taylor contributed directly to all three Lions touchdowns, including a decisive 2-yard pass to Carson Wall with 4:41 remaining in the third quarter. Mountain View's Brigham Moses opened their scoring with a thrilling 74-yard kickoff return, while Hyrum Stafford connected with Koa Giles for a 46-yard touchdown pass to give the Bruins a first-quarter lead. However, Payson's defense held firm in the fourth quarter to secure the win, leaving Mountain View scoreless in the final period.

Lone Peak (1-0) kicker Zachary Zolman played a pivotal role in his team's 33-21 nonregion victory over Crimson Cliffs. Zolman connected on field goals from 50, 30, and 25 yards, and converted all extra point attempts, accounting for 15 of his team's points. Lone Peak's Krew Robinson made a significant impact with an electrifying 99-yard kickoff return for a touchdown early in the third quarter, extending their halftime lead. After falling behind 27-0 midway through the third, Crimson Cliffs (0-1) rallied with a pair of fourth-quarter touchdown passes from Tanoai Andresen, but it wasn't enough to overcome the deficit. Despite the late effort, Crimson Cliffs couldn't break down Lone Peak's defensive resistance.

Lincoln Anderson was a standout for Copper Hills (1-0) as they cruised to a 29-0 shutout victory over Northridge in a nonregion matchup. Anderson contributed two field goals of 24 and 25 yards and successfully converted three extra-point attempts. The Grizzlies dominated offensively, with Ethan Hill connecting on touchdowns of 24 and 10 yards to Logan Beck in the second quarter. Ryder Mitchell added a 6-yard rushing touchdown with just 11 seconds left in the game to seal the comprehensive win. Northridge, now 0-1, struggled against Copper Hills' stifling defense and failed to score throughout the game.

American Fork (1-0) capitalized on a dominant fourth quarter to secure a 36-16 victory over Pleasant Grove in a nonregion matchup. Dalin Afu's 10-yard fumble recovery with 4:19 left in the game shut the door on any comeback attempt by the Vikings. American Fork's Jake Matsen connected with Zack Cowie for a 7-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter, extending their lead. Pleasant Grove briefly closed the gap in the fourth when Corbin Robbins electrified with a 94-yard kickoff return for a touchdown. However, American Fork's defense was pivotal, including a 64-yard interception return by Noah Behm in the third quarter, helping them maintain control after the first quarter.

Murray (1-0) defeated Uintah (0-1) 49-39 in a nonregion matchup highlighted by explosive passing plays from both offenses. The Spartans built a 28-7 halftime lead behind quarterback Dru Reuss, who connected with King Yom for a 68-yard touchdown and Jagger Karr for an 83-yard score in the fourth quarter. Uintah mounted a fourth-quarter rally, scoring 26 points in the final period as Landon Woods threw multiple touchdown passes and ran for a score, but the Utes fell short of completing the comeback.

Riverton (1-0) dominated West Jordan (0-1) in a nonregion matchup, rolling to a 35-17 victory. The Silverwolves' offense was efficient through the air, with Hayden Schneider connecting with Tavin Hill three times for touchdowns, including a 74-yard score in the third quarter. West Jordan scored first on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Kenyon Shockey to Lexen Rivera, but Riverton answered with 28 unanswered points by halftime. The Jaguars added a pair of second-half scores but couldn't overcome the early deficit.

Sky View edged Park City 13-10 in overtime in a defensive nonregion matchup. The Bobcats and Miners remained scoreless through the first half before Park City broke through with a 10-yard touchdown run by Ethan Cunningham late in the third quarter. Sky View answered in the fourth quarter as Tucker Stokes connected with Peyton Palmer on an 18-yard touchdown pass to tie the game. The contest extended to overtime where Park City's Knox Groenenboom kicked a field goal for the lead, but Palmer scored the decisive 6-yard rushing touchdown for Sky View.

Fremont dominated Weber in a nonregion matchup, winning 34-3. The Silverwolves scored on their first two possessions, with Ryder Wade breaking a 47-yard touchdown run at 1:12 of the first quarter before Calvin Cooper connected with Isaia Fonotisatele on a 73-yard touchdown pass just over four minutes later. Fremont's offensive onslaught continued with Fonotisatele returning a punt 55 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter, and the Silverwolves added touchdowns in the third and fourth quarters to put the game out of reach. Weber's only score came on a 35-yard field goal by Zach Jenkins in the second quarter.

Austin Cannon's explosive 55-yard touchdown reception from Cash Hawkins set the tone early as Viewmont (1-0) dominated in a 24-0 nonregion victory over Bonneville (0-1). The Vikings secured their win with a balanced attack, including Jesse Johnson's 2-yard TD run midway through the second quarter, and Miles Frey adding an 8-yard rushing score early in the third. Ethan Pitt extended the lead with a 30-yard field goal in the same quarter. Viewmont's defense was impenetrable, shutting out the Lakers throughout the game and ensuring a decisive victory.

Roy (1-0) dominated Taylorsville (0-1) in a nonregion game, securing a 54-7 victory that ended with a mercy rule. Roy's Alex Lasater capped the game with a 41-yard touchdown run with 1:30 left in the fourth quarter. Gunner Pearson led the Royals' aggressive offense with four rushing touchdowns, including a 54-yard sprint in the first quarter. Howie Howard contributed with three touchdowns, including a 65-yard run early in the third quarter. Taylorsville managed their sole score in the first quarter but couldn't find the end zone afterward. The Royals' defense held strong, shutting out the Warriors for the final three quarters.

American Leadership defeated Carbon 23-21 in double overtime on a 2-yard run by Mason Ober. The Eagles and Dinos traded scores throughout the game, and the teams were tied leading into the fourth quarter. Nick Ihli had a standout performance for American Leadership, catching a 75-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter and a 38-yard score in the third quarter.

Timpview's offense proved too much for Layton (0-1) in a nonregion matchup, with the Thunderbirds (1-0) building a 26-3 halftime lead en route to a 40-21 victory. TJ Tuha led the ground attack with multiple scoring runs, including a 41-yard touchdown in the third quarter, while Rob Tuaone returned an interception 45 yards for a score to extend Timpview's advantage. Layton rallied late with two touchdown passes from Tillman Thomas to Drew Godderidge in the fourth quarter, but the deficit proved too large to overcome.

North Sevier (1-0) scored early and often in a nonregion victory over Ben Lomond (0-1), taking a 28-7 halftime lead behind two first-quarter touchdown runs. The Wolves' defense forced a fumble that Chasen Woodside returned 45 yards for a score with 6:54 left in the second quarter. Ben Lomond rallied in the second half, scoring 26 unanswered points to pull within eight, but North Sevier's Houston Mickelsen scored on a 1-yard run with 10:11 remaining in the fourth quarter to seal the 41-33 win.

Cordon White starred for Richfield (1-0) in a dominant 62-20 nonregion victory over Dixie. White's performance included a 67-yard touchdown run and a 70-yard scoring pass to Trey Yardley, as well as a 27-yard touchdown pass to Shane Pearson. Richfield's explosive second quarter sealed the game, scoring 34 points, with White and Ngalu Taufatofua each contributing rushing touchdowns. Trey Yardley also shone in Richfield's defense, returning an interception 35 yards for a touchdown. Despite efforts from Dixie's Riker Muhlestein, who connected with Brygunn Soderquist for two touchdowns, the Flyers were unable to slow down the Wildcats' offensive barrage.

Timpanogos dominated Juan Diego in a nonregion matchup Friday night, with the Timberwolves (1-0) scoring on their first possession and never looking back in a 44-0 shutout. Logan Holloway orchestrated the offense efficiently, throwing three touchdown passes while also scoring on a 1-yard and 31-yard run. Ian Longhurst was a consistent target for Timpanogos, catching two scoring passes of 48 and 39 yards. The Soaring Eagle (0-1) failed to get on the scoreboard as Timpanogos' defense controlled the line of scrimmage throughout the game.

Silas Taumoepeau powered Westlake in their 42-21 nonregion win over Highland with a standout performance, throwing three touchdown passes. Westlake (1-0) fell behind early as Highland (0-1) scored twice in the first quarter, but quickly regrouped with a 42-yard touchdown pass from Taumoepeau to Kylan Xoumphonphackdy. Dylan Blakey's rushing ability was crucial, as he punched in two touchdowns on the ground, including an 11-yard score in the third quarter to extend Westlake's lead. Highland was unable to score again until the final quarter, when Will Bauman managed a late touchdown. Malik Sika's 57-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter sealed the win for the Thunder.

Delta (1-0) defeated Juab (0-1) 29-26 in a nonregion matchup, marking the Rabbits' first win over the Wasps since 2017. Bodey Shurtz scored the go-ahead touchdown with 4:54 remaining in the fourth quarter on a 1-yard run, giving Delta the final margin. Delta built a 14-7 lead after the first quarter before Juab rallied with 12 points in the third quarter to take a 26-21 advantage. The Rabbits' defense held the Wasps scoreless in the fourth quarter to secure the victory. Price Armstrong led Juab's offense with multiple touchdown passes, including a 58-yard score to Bryson Downard in the first quarter.

Tafuna, American Samoa Football (1-0) dominated East in a nonregion matchup Friday night, shutting out the Leopards 46-0 before the game ended with 9:14 remaining in the fourth quarter under the UHSAA's 44-point mercy rule. The visitors scored in every quarter, with 12 points in the first, 16 in the second and 12 in the third before adding six 

North Sanpete (1-0) dominated Cottonwood (0-1) in a non-region game Thursday, winning 57-0 and triggering the UHSAA's 44-point mercy rule at the end of the third quarter. The Hawks scored five touchdowns in the first quarter alone, with Chaetton Osborne, Trexon Madsen, and Seth Burningham each finding the end zone. Jesse Nuttall hauled in a 68-yard touchdown pass from Luke Lee in the 3rd quarter to extend the lead to 50-0 at halftime. Trevor Mann rushed for 157 yards to pace North Sanpete's ground game as the Hawks' offense was in complete control throughout the night.

Jaxon Pehrson led Corner Canyon (1-0) to a commanding 51-14 nonregion victory over Davis on Friday night, passing for 206 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for 103 yards. This marked the debut win for Corner Canyon head coach Casey Sutera. A decisive 30-point third quarter cemented the Chargers' dominance, highlighted by Diesel Dart's 63-yard touchdown reception and Jaxon Pehrson's 82-yard touchdown run. Corner Canyon's defense held Davis to 268 total yards, while the Chargers amassed 460 yards of offense. Despite a late 28-yard touchdown pass from Davis's Brodie Scheinberg to Bode Sparrow, Davis struggled to keep pace in the second half.

In Deer Creek's inaugural game, the Riverhawks were overrun by Mountain Crest (1-0), succumbing 49-0 under Utah's new 44-point mercy rule. Quarterback Brady Muir led the Mustangs with precision, throwing for three touchdowns, including a 72-yard bomb to Tanner Harris late in the third quarter. Muir's efforts in the first half set the tone, connecting with Kael Olsen for touchdowns of 44 and 8 yards, contributing to a 28-point first quarter. The nonregion matchup saw Mountain Crest's dominance early, with Tayton Page and Brock Hunter adding rushing touchdowns. The Riverhawks, playing their first-ever game, struggled to find their footing against an experienced Mustangs squad.

Enterprise (0-1) made a bold decision to go for a two-point conversion after Jake Christensen's 11-yard touchdown run with 1:27 left in the game, but the attempt failed, allowing North Summit (1-0) to escape with a 14-13 nonregion win. North Summit's Jaden Rowser electrified the field with a 58-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, while Knox Woolstenhulme contributed a 1-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter. Christensen produced both of Enterprise's touchdowns on the ground, including a 4-yard run in the second quarter. Despite a late surge, Enterprise was unable to overcome their one-point deficit.

Ridgeline (1-0) rolled past Morgan 42-28 in a nonregion matchup Friday night, with Noah Fiebia accounting for three touchdowns on the ground for the RiverHawks. Morgan (0-1) kept pace early, with Krew Asay returning an interception 42 yards for a score in the first quarter, but Ridgeline pulled away by halftime with a 28-7 advantage. The Trojans rallied in the third quarter with two scores to cut the deficit, but couldn't complete the comeback. Morgan's final score came with 10 seconds remaining when Webster Gilson threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to George Thurston.

Providence Hall (0-1) was shut out in its season opener, falling 29-0 to Pahrump, Nev. in a nonregion matchup. The Trojans scored 15 points in the second quarter and added a touchdown in each of the final two quarters to pull away from the visiting Patriots.

Owen Morris kicked a 21-yard field goal with 12 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter to lift Farmington (1-0) past Bingham (0-1) in a defensive nonregion contest. The Phoenix trailed 8-3 entering the final quarter before Morris connected on a 39-yard field goal earlier in the third quarter and Ty Runyan caught a 28-yard touchdown pass from Alton Dahl to give Farmington an 11-8 lead. Bingham's Beckham Greaves scored on a 3-yard reception from Knox Dawson with 6:49 left in the game to briefly take the lead, but Morris' game-winning kick proved decisive.

Kami Vaenuku powered into the end zone with a 3-yard touchdown run with just 4 seconds remaining in the game to lift Tooele (1-0) to a dramatic 14-10 victory over Union (0-1) in a nonregion matchup. The scoring play capped a thrilling comeback after Union took a brief lead with a 6-yard touchdown pass from Cruz Labrum to Reid Burgess at the start of the fourth quarter and a subsequent 27-yard field goal by Bryson Winterton with 2:33 left. Gus Pater put Tooele on the scoreboard first with an 18-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter. Tooele's defense held strong, preventing any scoring from Union until the final quarter.

Clearfield dominated Cyprus in a nonregion matchup, winning 24-7. The Falcons twice in the first quarter, with Micah Salazar breaking free for a 70-yard touchdown run and Bryson Ridge adding a 3-yard score in the first quarter. Ridge later returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown in the third quarter to put the game out of reach. Cyprus Pirates managed only a 4-yard touchdown run by Cody Campbell at the end of the opening quarter.

Logan (1-0) secured a debut win for new head coach Justin Hugie with a thrilling 25-21 comeback victory over Summit Academy in a nonregion game. Royce Sargent clinched the win with a 2-yard touchdown run with just 17 seconds remaining, capping off a remarkable fourth-quarter surge for the Grizzlies. Logan trailed 21-3 early in the final period but rallied with three touchdowns, including two scoring plays involving Sargent and quarterback Easton Favero. Summit Academy (-1) initially took the lead in the first quarter with a 19-yard touchdown pass from Rigby Young to Beckham Meredith and maintained it until the final minutes. The Bears added another touchdown from Young to Meredith in the fourth, but it wasn't enough to fend off Logan's late charge.

Jay Thompson powered Brighton (1-0) to a dominant 34-0 nonregion victory over West Field with a pair of short touchdown runs. Thompson opened the scoring with a 1-yard run in the first quarter and added a 2-yard score in the third quarter. The Bengals' balanced attack was complemented by Moises Cendejas, who found the end zone with a 4-yard rush in the second quarter. Adam Price chipped in with two field goals, including a 23-yarder in the fourth quarter, sealing the shutout. Brighton's defense stifled the Longhorns, keeping them scoreless throughout the contest.

Preston Ferran threw four touchdowns and rushed for another as the Titans (1-0) cruised to a 49-14 nonregion win over Cedar Valley (0-1) in Casey Evans' debut as head coach. Olympus dominated early, scoring 35 unanswered points in the first quarter, highlighted by Beckham Allred's 65-yard touchdown run just three minutes into the game. Sam Brown contributed defensively with a 32-yard interception return for a touchdown. Cedar Valley found the end zone in the second half with Keali'i Sisouphanh recording both their touchdowns, including a 40-yard pass from Cash Thacker. Despite the Aviators' late efforts, Olympus maintained a substantial lead, keeping Cedar Valley's comeback hopes at bay.

Coy Doman passed for 450 yards and four touchdowns as Pine View (1-0) took a commanding 44-28 nonregion victory over Manti. Doman's performance included a crucial 63-yard touchdown pass to Russell Jacobs in the fourth quarter, extending the Panthers' lead to 16 points with 5:22 remaining. Despite Manti's Trever Christensen catching a 38-yard touchdown from Kingston Wright in the final quarter, Pine View's offensive dominance proved too much for the Templars. The Panthers scored 21 points in the third quarter alone, highlighted by Max Yocham's 47-yard touchdown run. Ray Hosner marked his return as Pine View's head coach with an impressive season-opening win.

Syracuse's Kao Prom scored a dramatic 1-yard touchdown with 1:24 remaining, but the Titans (0-1) fell short of a comeback as their two-point conversion attempt failed, allowing Woods Cross (1-0) to secure a 27-26 victory in a nonregion game. Syracuse struck first with a 43-yard touchdown pass from Ledger Wight to Kaleb Hall in the opening quarter, and extended the lead in the second quarter through a Parker Moffat reception. However, Woods Cross responded with a 21-point second quarter, highlighted by a 63-yard touchdown pass from Tage Ita to Teiyon Halbasch. Ita also contributed a 1-yard rushing touchdown. Despite Syracuse's late surge with a touchdown pass to Bo Metcalfe in the fourth quarter, Archer Gale's pair of second-half field goals made the difference for Woods Cross.

Herriman (1-0) running back Filisi Filipe had a dominant performance, scoring three touchdowns including a 73-yard run with 1:14 remaining in the fourth quarter to seal a 25-14 nonregion victory over Bountiful (0-1). The Mustangs built a 19-0 lead by halftime, with Filipe scoring on runs of 54 and 2 yards in the opening half. Bountiful scored twice in the fourth quarter, with Madden Parks punching in a 3-yard touchdown run and Hudson Malmrose connecting with Max Feller on a 38-yard touchdown pass, but it was too little too late.

West (1-0) scored the go-ahead touchdown with 1:14 left in the fourth quarter when Dovani Dixon rushed 4 yards for a score, lifting the Panthers to a 20-14 nonregion victory over Arbor View, Nev. West struck first as Monson Vaenuku caught a 31-yard touchdown pass from Kamden Lopati with 1:17 remaining in the first quarter. Arbor View answered with a touchdown in the second quarter before West's Naeata Hamilton scored on a 3-yard run to give the Panthers a 14-7 halftime lead.

Snow Canyon outlasted Spanish Fork in a triple-overtime thriller, with Parker Olson connecting with Brody Lounsbury on the go-ahead two-point conversion in the third overtime period for the 64-62 nonregion victory. Olson passed for 402 yards and five touchdowns in the high-scoring affair, while Spanish Fork's Nixon Warren caught 10 passes for 268 yards and five touchdowns in the losing effort. The Warriors trailed 14-7 after the first quarter but kept pace throughout the back-and-forth contest, which remained close through regulation before heading to overtime. Spanish Fork scored first in triple OT, but missed its two-point conversion. Brody Lounsbury tied it with a 13-yard TD run, and then won it with the ensuing two-point conversion.

Alta (1-0) defeated Springville (0-1) 38-35 in a nonregion matchup Thursday night. The Red Devils dominated the third quarter, scoring 28 points to take a commanding lead before the Hawks rallied in the fourth. Alta scored twice in the final quarter, with Trever Cooke's 6-yard touchdown run with 3:28 remaining providing the go-ahead score. Springville's explosive third quarter, highlighted by an 80-yard touchdown pass from Beckett Burton to Sam Nadauld, proved insufficient as Alta's late offensive push secured the victory.

Box Elder (1-0) dominated Deseret Peak (0-1) in a nonregion matchup, winning 49-0 and enforcing the new UHSAA 44-point mercy rule. Kadyn Reyes sparked the Bees' offense with a 53-yard touchdown pass to Rhet Richards in the first quarter and added his own 23-yard rushing touchdown. The Bees jumped to a 27-0 lead in the first quarter and continued their control with both passing and rushing scores. Trace Tucker added a 3-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, contributing to Box Elder's comfortable halftime lead of 40-0. Tytan Hupp's 42-yard field goal in the fourth quarter capped off the scoring before the mercy rule concluded the game. Deseret Peak struggled offensively, failing to score throughout the contest.

Hurricane dominated Virgin Valley, Nevada, in a nonregion matchup, rolling to a 47-12 victory on the road. The Tigers scored 21 points in the second quarter to seize control early, with Titan Borchardt accounting for two touchdowns—a 48-yard pass reception and a 29-yard run. RJ Allred added two rushing touchdowns for Hurricane, while Drake Gines also scored on the ground.

Grantsville (1-0) overcame an early deficit to defeat San Juan 30-20 in a non-region game. San Juan struck first with two touchdowns in the opening quarter, but Grantsville answered with 13 unanswered points in the second quarter, including a 9-yard scoring run by Carter Bell. Bell added two more rushing touchdowns in the second half to put the Cowboys in control. San Juan briefly challenged late when Brigg Palmer caught a 39-yard touchdown pass from Beau Yeomans with 5:25 left in the fourth quarter but it was not enough.

Davis Carter's impressive efforts were not enough for Beaver (0-1) as they fell to Moapa Valley in a nonregion game, 27-21. Carter scored three touchdowns, including two rushing scores in the second quarter at 8:25 and 1:12, which temporarily put Beaver ahead 15-7. However, the Pirates responded with a strong third quarter, putting up 14 points to seize control of the game. Moapa Valley added another touchdown in the fourth quarter to secure their victory. Carter also connected with Emmet Lurth for a 24-yard touchdown pass with 15 seconds left in the third quarter, but Beaver couldn't find the end zone in the final quarter, sealing their fate.

Lincoln County, Nev. defeated Parowan (0-1) 35-28 in a nonregion matchup. The Lynx built an early lead with 12 points in the first quarter and 8 

Orem (1-0) started their season with a strong defensive performance, defeating Kamehameha, Hawaii 16-7 on the road. The Tigers secured the victory late in the game with Brooks Ross catching a pivotal 21-yard touchdown pass from Rock Speredon with 9:37 remaining in the fourth quarter. This added to JaVoni Halalilo's 60-yard interception return for a touchdown, which gave Orem an early lead in the first quarter. Adrian Sanchez chipped in with a 29-yard field goal in the third quarter. Despite Kamehameha tying the game at 7-7 with a score in the second quarter, they were unable to overcome Orem's defensive tenacity, failing to find the end zone again.

Milford (1-0) dominated Whitehorse (0-1) in a 1A 8-player matchup, scoring 52 points through three quarters to invoke the 44-point mercy rule. Braxton Hansen orchestrated the Tigers' offensive onslaught, throwing touchdown passes to Tayon Blackburn (29 yards and 5-yard run), Kasen Smith (7 yards) and Kamdon Spaulding (41 yards) while also adding a 37-yard rushing touchdown. Milford built a commanding 38-7 lead after the first quarter and extended it to 52-7 by the end of the third quarter, limiting the Raiders to a single score for the entire game.

Utah Military Camp Williams (1-0) opened its season with a 27-22 victory over Panguitch in a 1A 8-player nonregion contest.

Grand (1-0) defeated Water Canyon (0-1) 53-38 in a 1A 8-player nonregion matchup, with Beto Carroll leading the Red Devils' offensive attack. Carroll caught three touchdown passes from Justin Kimmerle, including a 49-yard score in the third quarter and a 27-yard reception with 6:15 left in the fourth quarter. Water Canyon jumped to a 22-8 lead after one quarter behind Deagan Williams, who threw touchdown passes to Gabe Cooke on plays of 88 and 77 yards, but Grand outscored the Wildcats 45-16 the rest of the way. Kimmerle connected with four different receivers for touchdowns to pace Grand's balanced attack.

Cedar City (1-0) opened its season with a 29-19 victory over Wasatch in a nonregion game. The Reds scored 14 points in the second quarter to build an early lead, with Cody Stevenson catching an 80-yard touchdown pass from Jackson Mann. Wasatch kept pace early behind a 55-yard field goal from Austin Wilde and an 80-yard scoring run by Bryce Harr in the second quarter. Cedar City pulled away in the second half with two touchdown passes from Mann to Hunter Burgess, including a 67-yard score in the fourth quarter that sealed the win.

Stansbury (1-0) opened its season with a 14-10 victory over Skyline in a defensive struggle. The Stallions scored twice in the second half, with Lincoln Reutzel catching touchdown passes from Brighton Reutzel of 4 yards in the third quarter and 9 yards with 7:22 remaining in the fourth. Skyline (0-1) got on the board first with a 27-yard field goal by Matthew Payne, then added a 38-yard touchdown pass from Tate Johnson to Tu'i Will with 35 seconds left in the first half, but couldn't find the end zone again. The nonregion matchup was decided in the final quarter as Stansbury's offense pulled away.

Mountain Ridge (1-0) opened its season with a dominant 41-26 nonregion victory over Skyridge (0-1). Jaxon Hunt orchestrated the Sentinels' offense, throwing four touchdown passes including an 82-yard strike to Xander Thayer in the second quarter. Bradley Foster rushed for 216 yards and added two touchdowns for Mountain Ridge. Skyridge kept pace early, with Jagger Fountaine throwing three touchdown passes, but Mountain Ridge pulled away with 28 points over the final two quarters.

title: Caitlin Clark makes WNBA history and breaks multiple records in one game during latest Indiana Fever win
description: Caitlin Clark is no stranger to making history, and she broke three records in the Indiana Fever win against the Dallas Wings. Caitlin Clark seems to be heating up at exactly the right time for the Indiana Fever.
fullText:
Caitlin Clark is no stranger to making history, and she broke three records in the Indiana Fever win against the Dallas Wings.

Caitlin Clark seems to be heating up at exactly the right time for the Indiana Fever. The team has been collecting wins consistently, and they added another big one on Friday.

While the team success is phenomenal, it was a momentous night for Caitlin, too. The 24-year-old managed to break all kinds of records with her performance.

When truly generational stars come through in any league, the records start falling at a rapid rate. And it's safe to say that CC is generational.

The Fever guard racked up 29 points, 10 assists, and shot over 60 percent from the field. She also only had one turnover, a phenomenal offensive display. And she ended up breaking three different records.

This was Clark's 20th game with 20 or more points and 10 or more assists. No other WNBA player has even 10, extending CC's lead in this metric. The next one is somehow even more impressive.

This win was Clark's 83rd game in the WNBA. The Iowa alum has already racked up her 700th career assist. This makes her the fastest player to hit that mark in the W this century. Incredibly, no NBA player can claim to have done so since 2000 either.

It was also her seventh game with more than 25 points this season. That is a mark no other point guard has reached in the league's history until now.

CC is already a huge fan favourite, and her playing well is excellent for the league. If she carries this form into the postseason, the WNBA playoffs will be must-see TV, to say the least.

title: Edwin Díaz survives another ninth-inning adventure as Dodgers beat Brewers
description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers wanted a clean ending Friday night.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers wanted a clean ending Friday night.

With a two-run lead and another save opportunity in front of him, Díaz turned the ninth inning at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium into another late-night test of the Dodgers' collective blood pressure. He hit a batter, walked two, struggled to locate his fastball and surrendered a 104-mph ground ball.

Bases loaded in the 9th inning, and Edwin Diaz managed to close out the game.

LA wins 3-1 @SportingTrib pic.twitter.com/RkxRC45gEU

Díaz got the final out on a grounder to Mookie Betts, preserving a 3-1 Dodgers victory over the Milwaukee Brewers and securing his seventh save since joining the Dodgers. It was hardly the type of save Díaz or the Dodgers would draw up, but after Thursday's disappointing loss to Milwaukee, the result was all that mattered.

"It wasn't pretty," Dave Roberts said. "I watched the inning too, but he made a pitch when he needed to."

That pitch came with two outs and the bases loaded.

Díaz had thrown 26 pitches in the inning, only 11 of them strikes. His fastball command deserted him, and Milwaukee kept the inning alive long enough to put the tying run on base. But Díaz stayed in the game, battled through the final hitter and finally induced the grounder that ended the threat.

"Even with that last hitter, I wanted to see him try to fight through it and get through it, so I was happy that he finished what he started," Roberts said.

For Díaz, the rough inning was another reminder that something has not quite been right mechanically. He said he has identified the issue as his posture and arm angle, with his arm angle getting lower than he wants.

"Yeah, they told me that my arm angle was a little bit low, so I was trying to work on that a little bit today," Díaz said. "My posture is the main focus in that."

Still, Díaz believes the work is moving him in the right direction.

"I'm going in a good direction right now," he said.

The Dodgers will give him a little more time to work on it. Roberts said Díaz will not be available for the next couple of games, allowing him to use the break to make adjustments with the pitching and strength staffs.

The Dodgers needed Díaz because they had built another narrow lead thanks to a combination of timely offense and another strong outing from Yoshinobu Yamamoto.

Yamamoto was electric from the start, limiting the Brewers to one run over six innings while striking out nine. He allowed four hits and two walks, throwing 97 pitches, 69 for strikes.

The Dodgers took an early lead in the first when Betts lined an RBI single to left, scoring Andy Pages.

Milwaukee answered, but Pages put the Dodgers back in front in the fifth.

Pages crushed his 20th home run of the season, a solo shot that gave the Dodgers a 2-1 advantage. It was another milestone in what has become an increasingly productive season for the young outfielder.

Interestingly, Pages has been perfectly balanced in the power department at home and on the road: 10 homers at Dodger Stadium and 10 on the road.

Then Tommy Edman added some breathing room in the sixth with his fourth home run of the season, pushing the Dodgers' lead to 3-1.

Tommy Edman hits the @Dodgers second homer of the night to extend their lead! pic.twitter.com/qgOZ6gjn0z

That was enough for the pitching staff, barely.

Evan Phillips worked a perfect seventh on 18 pitches before Tanner Scott followed with a scoreless eighth. Then came Díaz, and another ninth inning that seemed determined to make a routine save anything but routine.

And in doing so, they moved to 74-49, maintaining an eight-game lead over the Padres in the National League West.

The Brewers remain one game ahead of the Dodgers for the best record in baseball, with two games still remaining between the National League's top two teams this weekend.

The Dodgers would certainly prefer those games to end a little more quietly. But on Friday, after the way Thursday night ended, they were happy to take the win, even if Díaz made them sweat for every last out.

title: A small Texas company’s bid to create a Greenland oil boom—and a Dr. Phil documentary—is delayed but undaunted
description: Greenland Energy is facing almost 18 months of delays, but plans to drill for oil as soon as late 2027.
fullText:
Amid the tensions spurred by President Donald Trump's proclaimed desire to annex Greenland, one Texas driller made plans to create an oil boom along the Danish territory's sparsely populated east coast. But those aspirations are now facing repeated delays in the face of regulatory and community pushback.

The first test well was slated to be drilled this summer with a camera crew overseen by producer Phil "Dr. Phil" McGraw to document the effort. As local opposition escalated and permitting slowdowns took hold, the drilling was delayed to the winter—upon the government's request—and now, after an additional kerfuffle this week concerning the movement of drilling equipment, the project was further pushed back until the end of 2027, essentially an 18-month delay.

Oil drilling is especially sensitive in Greenland where there's a climate change-related moratorium on licensing, though the Texas company is essentially operating by means of a grandfathered loophole. The situation has become more delicate still as the White House repeatedly signals it wishes to take over the massive icy territory in order to tap petroleum and critical minerals.

But Robert Price, the CEO of Texas-based Greenland Energy, exclusively told Fortune he is disappointed but undeterred, and he remains as bullish as ever about Greenland's oil prospects.

"It was very frustrating. We've had some ups and downs in the last week or so," Price said. "We actually had much of the equipment being mobilized. And when we got word from the government, we shut down the mobilization. We had a drilling rig in in Calgary that was en route to Montreal. So there were some sunken costs. A lot of those costs will be able to be used for the next drilling season."

Wall Street was disappointed though. Since going public in March on the Nasdaq Global Market, Greenland Energy's market cap has plunged nearly 85% down to about $54 million. But Price insists the company is stable.

"We preserved a lot of cash on hand. Financially, we're still very sound," the veteran oilman said.

The Greenland government requested the company drill in the winter instead of the summer for environmental purposes. "The birds have already migrated. The tundra will not be disturbed. We'll be able to go literally over it when it's iced up," Price said.

On the downside, helicopter evacuations and harsher weather are trickier during the winter months. "The winter can be unpredictable in the Arctic Circle, and so we do worry about the health and safety of our people if someone got injured, being able to get them out," Price added.

title: Low water in Rome’s drought-hit Tiber river exposes ancient ruins of Nero’s Bridge
description: Scorching temperatures and a long, dry summer have given locals and tourists alike a rare opportunity to see the remains of a 2,000-year-old bridge that once spanned the Tiber river that weaves throug...
fullText:
Scorching temperatures and a long, dry summer have given locals and tourists alike a rare opportunity to see the remains of a 2,000-year-old bridge that once spanned the Tiber river that weaves through the center of Rome.

The flow of the Tiber, which is fed from tributaries from the northern Apennine Mountains, has fallen below 80 cubic meters a second, half the national average for this time of year, according to Rome's civil protection coordinator, Giovanni Giganti. "We are facing a major water crisis. And it is a crisis that is also due to the fact that this winter we did have quite abundant rainfall, but then the dry periods … were quite long," Giganti told the Associated Press.

Nero's Bridge (Pons Neronianus) was thought to have been built as a triumphal monument by the Emperor Caligula around 39 AD. But it is referred to as Nero's Bridge because Nero, Caligula's nephew, renamed a number of ancient structures after himself during his rule from 54 to 68 AD, according to historical accounts.

The bridge originally connected the ancient Campus Martius area, which now houses the Spanish Steps, the Piazza del Popolo and the posh shopping streets around Via Condotti, to the Circus of Nero stadium where St. Peter was martyred and upon which St. Peter's Basilica and the Vatican City now stand.

The remnants of the structure can best be seen from the Bridge of Angels, which leads to Castel Sant' Angelo near Vatican City.

The bridge is usually entirely underwater, but this year full blocks of the ancient structure are visible, giving archaeologists a rare opportunity to study it.

The Tiber's low water level has also turned up e-bikes and scooters, refrigerators and even a car further upstream. The last time the remains of the bridge were visible was during a similar drought in 2022.

title: 'Master manipulator' murder suspect Isabelle Johnson arrested
description: Isabelle Johnson has been charged with the murder of a 43-year-old man.
fullText:
Isabelle Johnson, a suspected murderer who authorities say had been using multiple disguises and identities, has been arrested and taken into custody, according to the Walton County Sheriff's Office.

"We got her," officials said in a post on social media late Thursday. "Isabelle Johnson is in custody."

Johnson, 38, has been charged with the murder of 43-year-old Jason Christopher Coulthart who was found dead in a shallow grave in June in Florida after he had gone missing in May, according to the Walton County Sheriff's Office.

Investigators say Johnson used multiple identities to evade authorities, calling her a "master manipulator."

Coulthart was reported missing on May 24 after he was last seen leaving the College Condominiums complex in Florida, according to the sheriff's office.

Unidentified remains were found on a Freeport, Florida, property on June 25 -- after investigators were able to identify where Coulthart's body had been buried, according to the sheriff's office.

A DNA match confirmed the remains were Coulthart's in July, the sheriff's office said.

Five others have been arrested and charged in connection with the murder, including two people accused of aiding Johnson evade investigators, the sheriff's office said.

title: Trump says he will soon declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory
description: President Trump said he plans to declare the Strait of Hormuz a U.S. territory as he once again asserted control of the critical waterway.
fullText:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump said he plans to soon declare the Strait of Hormuz "a territory of the United States" as he once again asserted U.S. control of the critical waterway amid the war in Iran.

Trump made the extraordinary remark as he touted the success of an American naval blockade of Iranian ports that he claims has demonstrated U.S. control of the strait, a major accessway for oil shipping in the Middle East.

"After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States," Trump said in an Aug. 14 speech in Garden City, New York. "Essentially that's what we have. We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to."

More: Trump rejects criticism of USS Lincoln, says deployment 'not long enough'

It was unclear whether Trump's comments marked a new policy position or just his latest escalation in rhetoric over the Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman along the coasts or Iran and Oman. Trump claims the United States has opened the strait to all commercial ships other than those from Iran, crippling Iran's economy because of its reliance on oil exports.

Iran has rejected Trump's characterization of the strait, asserting it is instead under the "complete management and control" of Iran and that no commercial ships can go through without Iran's permission.

Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran's deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, quickly rejected Trump's latest comments.

"The Strait of Hormuz cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor by an election speech. Iran neither fears threats nor cowers before displays of power," Gharibabadi said in a statement.

Since a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran to negotiate an end to war fell apart in July, Iran has resumed attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz that Gharibabadi says does not have permission to access the channel. The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran for Aug. 13 drone strikes on two tankers as they sailed through the Strait of Hormuz.

Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth has said the U.S. military has the capability to maintain a naval presence "indefinitely" in the Middle East to enforce its blockade of Iran.

"Indefinitely, the United States Navy can maintain a blockade like that because we'll rotate ships in and out, as we have, and we'll continue to," Hegseth told reporters Aug. 13 during a trip to Panama.

In his remarks in New York, Trump also addressed high gas prices as a result of the war in Iran, saying he will "never apologize" for his decision to attack Iran and arguing the cause of the war is worth the higher costs.

The high gas prices, which remain above $4 nationally for a gallon of regular gas, pose a major problem politically for Republicans ahead of the November midterm elections.

"For you to pay a tiny, little bit more for you're gasoline, just remember," Trump said, it's so "a very evil country" can't have a nuclear weapon.

"When you have to pay a little bit more, you're at $4, it's OK ‒ I mean, I will never apologize, I did the right thing," Trump said. "You just have to remember that what we're doing is a great service for the world."

Reach Joey Garrison on X @joeygarrison.

title: Search underway for 'tomb raiders' suspected of stealing from cemeteries in 9 states
description: Police said the suspects are a man, his girlfriend and her mother.
fullText:
A search is underway for a trio of "tomb raiders" that have allegedly traveled the country visiting local cemeteries, stealing family heirlooms out of niches containing cremated remains.

Arrest warrants have been issued for Drake Lee Milam, 33; his girlfriend, Porsche Bancroft, 32; and her mother, Angela Garrett, 52. Florida is seeking to extradite them to face charges in this case, according to the Orange County Sheriff's Office.

Man charged with attempted murder after hitting woman with hammer

The suspects, who live in Indianapolis, are believed to have hit at least nine states, the sheriff's office said.

This includes Oklahoma, Minnesota, Texas, Georgia, Iowa, North Carolina and New York, according to the sheriff's office.

"Imagine losing your wife or husband and placing their wedding ring, and yours, in the niche -- only to have them stolen by thieves looking for an easy payday," the sheriff's office said in a statement.

There are 20 cases of robberies in Florida, but detectives believe there could be "many more," the sheriff's office said.

Suspect believed to have killed father, set home ablaze arrested after manhunt

"What a horrible person you are if you decide to steal from the dead," Cpl. Cole Brazee said in a video posted by the sheriff's office on social media.

"Please check your loved one's resting place to make sure your prized heirlooms are safe. Our partners at Central Florida Crimeline agree that this is such a heinous crime that they are putting up a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to an arrest. 800-423-TIPS (8477)," the sheriff's office said.

title: 'Hey, buddy, I just crashed': Footage shows pilot walking away from fighter jet crash
description: The F/A-18 Hornet aircraft crashed in Washington in June.
fullText:
Dramatic new footage shows the moment local authorities encountered a pilot who had ejected from a fighter jet before it crashed into a mountainside in Washington state earlier this summer.

The F/A-18 Hornet aircraft slammed into a mountainside on June 13, in the area of Rimrock Lake, about 55 miles southeast of Seattle, sending a plume of black smoke into the air and igniting a wildfire.

The pilot assigned to Marine Aircraft Group 11, 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing, in Miramar, California, is seen with his face bloodied and appearing a little shaken up in the body camera footage released Friday by the Yakima County Sheriff's Office.

Army temporarily grounds all Apache helicopter flights after fatal crash

He is seen approaching deputies with his phone in his hand and 911 on the screen.

"What kind of jet is that?" the pilot is asked by one of the responders.

"That's an F-18," he replies. "Well, that was an F-18." He adds, "We were doing circles over the lake, doing some low-level training. ...And then I tucked in, and I'm not sure exactly."

"You hit the tree bad, bud," a witness states.

Later, the pilot is seen making a call to alert others to the wreck.

"Hey, buddy, I just crashed," the pilot says.

Later in the video, a parachute is seen hanging from a tree.

Responding officers with the sheriff's department said the pilot's injuries consisted of minor lacerations to his face.

In a news release at the time, the 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing said the pilot was conducting routine training when the aircraft experienced a "non-fatal aviation mishap."

The cause of the crash is still under investigation.

title: Congo says Ebola outbreak spreads to northeastern Bas-Uele province
description: DAKAR, Aug 14 () - The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of ‌Congo has spread to a ‌sixth province, Bas-Uele, located in the northeast of ​the country, the communications ministry said on Friday, ...
fullText:
DAKAR, Aug 14 (Reuters) - The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of ‌Congo has spread to a ‌sixth province, Bas-Uele, located in the northeast of ​the country, the communications ministry said on Friday, officially confirming a case discovered earlier.

Health authorities have identified a ‌person who ⁠has died from Ebola in the provincial capital Buta, an ⁠official from the National Institute for Biomedical Research told Reuters on Thursday.

Bas-Uele ​wasn't previously ​affected by ​the virus. The ‌new case raised fears that people who have been in contact with the patient may have also been infected.

Delayed detection, conflict and strained health ‌services have helped the ​virus spread more rapidly ​than in ​previous outbreaks.

The latest report, ‌published on the ministry's ​X account, ​said that the number of confirmed Ebola cases in Congo has ​increased to ‌4,665, including 2,184 deaths.

title: Count Binface receives over a quarter of votes in Clacton by-election
description: The dustbin themed candidate got 9,455 votes and came second to Nigel Farage
fullText:
Count Binface, the self-styled intergalactic space warrior, has received nearly 10,000 votes in the Clacton by-election, his best performance yet.

The much-photographed election veteran was the main rival to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage in an election race caused by Farage resigning, only to run again - which sparked a mass boycott by the other main UK parties.

Farage has re-won his seat, receiving more than 22,000 votes in Clacton, on the Essex coast.

Binface received 26.9% of the vote while Farage won 63.3%. Binface had his highest share yet with 9,455 votes, having lost to no fewer than three prime ministers, and one who later became prime minister, in previous attempts.

But how many votes has he previously received? And where does he fit into the British tradition of spoofing politicians?

The man inside the bin is the comedian Jon Harvey, an Oxford graduate who has specialised in satire, writing scripts for BBC comedy shows The Thick of It and Have I Got News For You.

He first donned a bin on his head to stand for election in 2017, when he challenged the then Prime Minister Theresa May in her Maidenhead constituency, although back then he was known as Lord Buckethead, a character inspired by a Star Wars parody film.

He won 249 votes and viral fame, leading to an appearance on John Oliver's HBO show Last Week Tonight - as well as a legal dispute with another Lord Buckethead he described at the time as "an unpleasant battle on the planet Copyright".

Harvey found himself a different bin to cover his head and switched characters to Count Binface to take on the next Conservative leader, Boris Johnson, announcing himself as the leader of the Recyclons from planet Sigma IX.

He only won 69 votes, but was again able to take his place on stage as the election result was declared alongside a sitting prime minister, who was also flanked by a candidate dressed as the Sesame Street character Elmo, at his Uxbridge election count.

A third Conservative leader, Rishi Sunak, was in Count Binface's sights in the 2024 general election campaign.

He got 308 votes, which at the time was his best result.

The Monster Raving Loony Party's candidate, Sir Archibald Stanton, received 99 votes - 0.2% of the vote share.

In June this year, it was Andy Burnham's turn to face Binface in the by-election that paved the way for the then Greater Manchester Mayor to become prime minister.

Rather than studiously ignoring the intergalactic warlord, as some may have been tempted to do, Burnham shook him warmly by the hand as he was elected Labour MP for Makerfield.

Binface bagged just 95 votes to Burnham's 24,927.

While Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election on Friday morning, Count Binface came second.

The Reform UK leader got 22,239 while Count Binface received 9,455. The intergalactic space warrior celebrated the number with his usual two peace sign fingers.

Speaking to BBC Breakfast after, Binface said: "I promised to be a local champion for Clacton and I thought to hear the verdict of the Clactonites was the least I could do."

The UK has a rich history of novelty candidates standing in elections, with Monster Raving Loony Party founder Screaming Lord Sutch - a rock musician who fought more than 40 elections in his trademark top hat and gold lame suit - first standing in a by-election in the 1960s. A different Lord Buckethead stood in 1987 and 1992, while comedian Al Murray's pub landlord stood against Farage in 2015.

Objections to such "frivolous" candidates date back even further - to 1918, when a £150 deposit was introduced for candidates. That was later upped to £500, in 1985, in large part due to the popularity of the Monster Raving Loony Party.

But the bar for entry remains fairly low: anyone over the age of 18 who can scrape together a £500 deposit and get support from 10 people in the form of signatures is allowed to stand as a candidate in UK elections.

That's why Count Binface has been able to stand in so many high-profile elections. He has, however, lost his £500 every time, after failing to meet the minimum 5% of votes cast in order for his deposit to be returned.

Yet Binface has had his moment in the spotlight each time.

That is because another British tradition means all election candidates must stand side-by-side on a stage at the election count to hear how many votes they have each received - it's a literal leveller, where everyone from prime minsters to a bloke dressed as a bin has the right to be seen and heard as an official candidate.

But all of these no-hope novelty candidates share a few serious aims: to poke fun at power, prick the pomposity of political elites, and allow people a protest vote.

Bart Scott says ESPN chose worst possible time to tell him he lost his job
description: Ryan Clark headlined ESPN’s first round of summer layoffs because ESPN chose to inform him by pulling him off the air from NFL Live on July 20. Bart Scott was also part of the layoffs, but he flew relatively under the radar, even though ESPN apparently informed him in a similarly ruthless way. “Hey, man,…
fullText:
Ryan Clark headlined ESPN's first round of summer layoffs because ESPN chose to inform him by pulling him off the air from NFL Live on July 20. Bart Scott was also part of the layoffs, but he flew relatively under the radar, even though ESPN apparently informed him in a similarly ruthless way.

"Hey, man, I was going into my radio show, and they called me, like, 'Hey, uh, just to let you know, wish we could do it in person,'" Scott said while appearing on The Joint Venture Show with Craig Carton and Lil Wayne this week. "Like, no, you don't, motherf*cker. 'Oh, I wish I could do it in person!' Nah. So, it's like, 'We're not gonna renew you.' My contract is expiring in September. So, I found out that way."

Despite the lack of respect, Scott explained why he didn't let the nature of his exit tarnish his entire tenure or his outlook on his future.

"It's part of the business," Scott said. "You understand the balance, and I don't know what they had to do when they had to trim the fat. I had never been there, where my contract was expiring, because usually when it's a year, I get renewed. But it's what it is, man. Sometimes, losing your job can be some of the biggest blessings because it forces you to try and do something else and, sometimes, step out of your comfort zone.

"Listen, one thing that is constant is change, and I've been fired before. I understand the process, and I hold no ill will. I don't even know who made the call. But I did enjoy my time there. I enjoyed using the platform, keeping myself relevant. I wasn't a first-round draft pick; I'm not a Hall of Famer. I think I was a pretty good player, but I just appreciate them giving me the platform, and I'm not gonna hold any ill will toward them. It's my job to make them regret it."

Scott entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent, signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2002. He became an impact linebacker with the Ravens (2002-08) and New York Jets (2009-2012). After retiring, Scott joined CBS Sports' NFL Today studio crew as an analyst. With Carton and Lil Wayne, Scott cited that experience as a precursor to understanding ESPN's decision to move on.

"I thought I was going to be able to work with Shannon [Sharpe]," Scott said. "But, sometimes, in this business — at least back then — they want shows to look a certain way."

"White?" Carton bluntly posited.

"Yeah, you can't have too many of us," Scott said. "Me and Shannon are similar. We represent a certain type of demographic. We're both funny, loud, loquacious, all that type of stuff, and I never got the opportunity."

Scott joined ESPN in a limited capacity on The Michael Kay Show on ESPN 98.7 in 2017, eventually becoming a full-time personality across ESPN platforms in 2020. He most recently co-hosted Bart & Carlin on ESPN New York and appeared on ESPN's Get Up! and First Take.
