title: Good Sports: Fresno dad turns hobby into unforgettable moment with Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott
description: A Fresno father's custom tribute hat for Dak Prescott turned a year-old painting hobby into an unforgettable, full-circle moment.
fullText:
A Fresno father's painting hobby led to an unforgettable encounter when Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott not only accepted one of his custom hats, but later wore it and sought out the artist behind it.

Mario Corona, a stay-at-home dad, licensed EMT and aspiring firefighter, began painting hats about a year ago. He said he never expected one of his designs would end up in the hands of an NFL quarterback.

"A day that I definitely won't forget," Corona said.

Recently, Corona completed a Dallas Cowboys collection that included a tribute to Prescott's brother, Jace. Prescott lost his brother to suicide in 2020 and has spoken publicly about raising awareness since then.

Corona created what he calls an "Angel Hat," featuring a portrait of Jace on the side.

"I know as a Cowboys fan, as a Dak fan, I know how much his brother meant to him and his motivation," Corona said.

Corona traveled to Cowboys training camp in Oxnard hoping to personally give the hat to Prescott. During First Responders Appreciation Day, he was able to get on the field.

"The players right in front of Dak were CeeDee [Lamb] and [George] Pickens, which were the players that were on my hat that I was wearing at the time. So I got caught up in trying to show them the hat I was wearing," Corona said. "By the time they passed and I turned back, Dak was already right here. I just babbled out whatever words were trying to come out of my mouth. Luckily, he did grab it before walking off."

Prescott accepted the hat without initially noticing the portrait painted on its side.

"I was happy that I knew he took it at least. I was actually leaving training camp pretty bummed. I didn't sell any hats, I didn't get any autographs," Corona said.

After leaving camp, Corona saw photos on social media showing Prescott wearing the hat. That is when he learned the quarterback was looking for the artist who created it.

"Got in the car, drove back... they're like, dude, you're going to have to go to the hotel," Corona said.

Corona later reunited with Prescott and captured the interaction on his Meta glasses.

"It was just real. It felt real," Corona said. "You know that moment was bigger than an autograph."

Throughout the remainder of training camp, Prescott was seen wearing Corona's hat.

The positive response to his work has encouraged Corona to take the next step with his business. He said he plans to open for commissions in November.

"As long as you're passionate about it and you stay dedicated... progress will come. If you're trying, you're going to have improvement. It for sure has paid off," Corona said.

title: Brittney Griner lands back on injury report before Sun-Liberty showdown
description: Connecticut could be without two crucial frontcourt players against surging New York
fullText:
Brittney Griner lands back on injury report before Sun-Liberty showdown originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Connecticut Sun may be staring at a brutal frontcourt problem before Saturday's matchup with the New York Liberty. Connecticut listed Brittney Griner as questionable because of a lingering left knee injury. Forward Aaliyah Edwards also received a questionable designation with a left ankle injury.

Losing either player would be damaging. Losing both against Breanna Stewart, Jonquel Jones and a surging Liberty team could leave the Sun facing one of their most difficult challenges of the season.

Connecticut will host New York at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday at Mohegan Sun Arena. The Sun enter the game at 8-24 after suffering their sixth loss in seven games, while the Liberty have won eight of their last 10.

Griner has been dealing with the knee issue for nearly a month. The 35-year-old center sustained the injury during Connecticut's 72-63 loss to the Phoenix Mercury on July 19. She played 31 minutes before exiting and subsequently missed four consecutive games.

Game Status Report vs. New York Liberty - 8.15.26

Aaliyah Edwards - QUESTIONABLE (Left Ankle)
Brittney Griner - QUESTIOABLE (Left Knee) pic.twitter.com/sKiS4TZ5Xu

Griner returned Aug. 7 against her former team and helped the Sun earn a much-needed victory over Phoenix. She played 24 minutes in that contest, but her workload has remained something to monitor. The nine-time All-Star was questionable before Thursday's game against the Atlanta Dream. Griner ultimately played, but she logged only 19 minutes and finished with five points, seven rebounds and four assists in a 104-69 loss.

Her remaining on the injury report suggests Connecticut is not yet comfortable declaring the knee issue resolved. Griner has played in only 18 of the Sun's first 32 games this season. Despite the interruptions, she is averaging 13.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks while shooting 52.7% from the field.

Those numbers prove she can still control stretches of games. The larger question is how often her body will allow her to do it.

Griner is not Connecticut's only frontcourt concern. Edwards also could miss Saturday's game because of a left ankle injury. Her presence would become even more important if Griner cannot play.

The Sun already face a significant size and rebounding challenge against New York. Jones remains one of the league's most imposing interior players, while Stewart can score from nearly anywhere on the floor. Connecticut needs Griner's rim protection to discourage drives and contest Jones around the basket. It needs Edwards' mobility and physicality to defend Stewart, rebound and create second opportunities.

Without both, the Sun could be forced to rely heavily on Olivia Nelson-Ododa and Raegan Beers while using smaller lineups for extended stretches.

That approach could improve Connecticut's pace, but it also would leave the team vulnerable on the glass and inside the paint. The Liberty have recently overwhelmed opponents with their rebounding. Giving Jones and Stewart repeated second-chance opportunities would be a recipe for another long afternoon.

Thursday's loss demonstrated how quickly games can get away from the Sun. Atlanta scored 104 points and won by 35. Angel Reese controlled the interior with 15 rebounds, while the Dream repeatedly turned Connecticut's defensive breakdowns into easy scoring opportunities.

Now the Sun must prepare for an opponent with even more proven offensive weapons. New York owns a 21-14 record and recently defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 85-81. The Liberty nearly squandered a 28-point fourth-quarter lead, but Sabrina Ionescu made critical free throws to secure the victory.

The Liberty are dealing with injury concerns of their own. Satou Sabally is out while recovering from lingering concussion symptoms, Leonie Fiebich is sidelined by a foot injury and Ionescu is listed as questionable with a foot issue. That creates at least some hope for Connecticut.

New York, however, still can turn to Stewart, Jones, Marine Johannès and a deep collection of experienced contributors. Johannès recently scored a career-high 27 points while hitting seven 3-pointers in a 111-71 victory over the Las Vegas Aces. Connecticut cannot spend the opening quarter attempting to find its energy. The Sun must defend with urgency, limit turnovers and establish some offensive rhythm before New York begins dictating the game.

Griner's final designation will affect almost every part of the Sun's game plan. If she plays, Connecticut can work through her in the post and force Jones to defend rather than allowing her to roam near the rim. Griner also gives the Sun a reliable target when their perimeter offense stalls.

Her defensive impact might be even more important. Griner's size allows Connecticut's guards to apply more pressure knowing an elite shot-blocker is stationed behind them.

If she sits, the Sun will have to play faster and generate more offense from their guards and wings. Saniya Rivers and Leila Lacan could receive increased responsibility, while Connecticut may rely more heavily on transition opportunities.

Neither option guarantees success against the Liberty.

That is what makes Griner's latest injury update so concerning. The Sun are not merely waiting to see whether one player will be available. They are waiting to learn which version of their team can take the floor.

MORE: Aliyah Boston makes emphatic MVP declaration about Fever teammate

Connecticut's 8-24 record makes a late playoff push increasingly unlikely. That reality should influence how the organization handles Griner.

The Sun would benefit from having their veteran center against New York, but risking further damage to her knee for one regular-season game would make little sense. Griner already has missed 14 games and recently returned from a four-game absence caused by the same injury.

Connecticut must determine whether she is truly ready for another physical matchup. If Griner plays, her minutes could remain limited. If she sits, the Sun will have to find another way to survive against one of the WNBA's strongest frontcourts.

Either way, Saturday's final injury report could shape the entire game before the ball is tipped.

title: Tagovailoa, Falcons offense struggle to get started in his brief Atlanta debut
description: Tua Tagovailoa faced heavy pressure in his two series of work Friday night against the Denver Broncos.
fullText:
Tua Tagovailoa's Falcons preseason debut Friday showed that he and the rest of Atlanta's offense have some work to do.

Granted, it was a brief outing, with Tagovailoa playing only two series with the starters in Atlanta against the Denver Broncos, and it wasn't the full lineup. Running back Bijan Robinson and right tackle Jawaan Taylor both sat out, and Drake London played only a few snaps.

But even against a good Denver defense that fielded some of its starting unit, the Falcons showed little of the firepower they're hoping for in the regular season, with their three main playmakers back.

On Tagovailoa's first series, the Falcons went three-and-out. He dropped a shotgun snap that hit him squarely in the hands, leading to a sack, and Atlanta punted one play later.

Tua fumbles the snap pic.twitter.com/hP5rsAzKom

The second series wasn't much better. The Broncos were getting pressure often, with Tagovailoa having to throw multiple passes away. He was hit hard on third down, which might have led head coach Kevin Stefanski to say no mas.

Tagovailoa finished his outing 3-for-5 passing for 22 yards. He targeted tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. on four of his five passes, often under duress.

With Michael Penix Jr. still out with injury, Cooper Rush replaced Tagovailoa and promptly was picked on his second pass attempt of the game.

It's hard to judge the Falcons' offensive performance in a vacuum Friday. The biggest eyesore was the pressure the offensive line surrendered, with Michael Jerrell replacing Taylor. The blocking wasn't great.

They'll want to get that ironed out before the next preseason game, and certainly prior to Week 1 against the Steelers. Tagovailoa needs all the clean pockets he can get if he wants to fend off Penix this whole season.

title: Mets' Juan Soto expects to return before end of season: 'Why not try to rejoin this team?'
description: Mets outfielder Juan Soto expressed his desire to return to the team before the end of the 2026 season as he continues his recovery from a left calf strain.
fullText:
Juan Soto, the Mets' biggest bat and their biggest star, has been out with a calf injury since late July, but wants to return to the team before the end of the 2026 season.

With New York's playoff chances dwindling after being sellers at the trade deadline, it would be understandable if Soto was shut down for the rest of the year as he recovers, but the Mets' lone All-Star this season vows to be back with this team.

"We are playing really good baseball right now," Soto told MLB.com ahead of Friday's series opener with the Nationals. "Why not try to rejoin this team? It would be really fun. It would be great for me and the team. [I want to] finish the season strong and keep the momentum for next year, too."

Entering play Friday, the Mets are 5-3 since the Aug. 3 trade deadline and are getting major contributions from the young kids and some recent call-ups.

But New York could use an infusion of Soto. Before this latest injury, Soto was having a Soto-like season. However, being available has been a challenge for Soto. The slugger has missed 38 games entering Friday between his first stint on the IL with a right calf strain and this current injury to his left leg.

Soto called his 2026 injuries "tough" and hopes to learn from this experience and stay healthy for his team moving forward.

"It's tough for me to lose so many games. I've never been on this side of it," Soto said. "I think it's good for me -- for my career -- because it will teach me a lot of things. I have to adjust in my training [and] conditioning to keep moving forward in a positive way. I have to learn about my body a little bit more, learning how it works and go from there."

In 84 games this season, Soto has slashed .283/.408/.539 with 21 home runs and 52 RBI en route to another All-Star Game selection.

And while the Mets have yet to give a timeline for Soto's return, the outfielder was doing pregame workouts at Citi Field, in good spirits.

Juan Soto does some work pregame and runs at Citi Field pic.twitter.com/UFxUYw1D0z

title: IndyCar President Doug Boles Furious About Safety At Markham
description: IndyCar Series President Doug Boles was strongly dissatisfied that the street course in Markham, Ontario was not completed and all Friday track action was cancelled.
fullText:
In what could have been a great opening day for IndyCar on the streets of Markham, Ontario turned into bitter disappointment for the huge throng of fans in the grandstands and for IndyCar President Doug Boles.

Instead of racing action, the only wheels turned on the 2.19-mile, 12-turn road course was construction machinery still trying to complete the track build. Without enough key tire packs in place to make for a safe impact area, IndyCar officials cancelled all track activity on Friday and issued a revised schedule for Saturday.

That left Boles furious that the track was not ready in time by the promoter of this weekend's event, and a key, longtime IndyCar ally, Green Savoree Promotions.

"IndyCar is incredibly disappointed that our promoter was not able to complete the track build on time, despite significant support from our team on site," Boles said. "Ontario has always been a magnificent market for our sport and the number of spectators that attended today is a shining example of that. New events can always pose logistical challenges and we join in the frustration of our loyal fans and apologize.

"Once we hit the track, we believe the circuit will be spectacular. We would like to thank the city of Markham for the major support it has made to provide IndyCar a layout, which is fast, technical and will put on a terrific show on Sunday."

There was a lot of excitement heading into the NTT IndyCar race at a new venue Friday on the streets of Markham, Ontario. The fans arrived early and filled the impressive grandstands, excited to witness IndyCar action in the buildup to Sunday's Ontario Honda Dealers Indy At Markham.

But the track wasn't ready and had some serious safety issues, including the lack of tire packs that are used as key safety barriers on street courses. They are needed for runoff areas and a few other places on track. The promoter had a plan in place to address that issue in time for Saturday morning's activity, according to IndyCar.

Other issues included a delay in the track build that included completing a full race track wall and fencing and significant safety concerns with areas of the wall and runoff.

Also, a lack of personnel to complete the tire and fence/wall construction.

The track build for the 2.19-mile, 12-turn street course race in Markham, Ontario began on July 19. The course is on the site of a GO Train station, which is still in use but the parking lots are the location of the double pit lane being used by INDYCAR. The parking lots closest to the pit lane were fully turned over to race promoters Green Savoree Promotions at end of day on Wednesday, August 12.

IndyCar continues to monitor the ongoing circuit construction by Green Savoree Racing Promotions.

IndyCar's Saturday schedule includes Practice 1 from 10-11:30 a.m. Eastern Time, televised on FS2, IndyCar Practice 2 from 2:30 to 4 p.m. on FS1 and Qualifying from 6:30 to 7 p.m. ET on FOX One, and 7-8 p.m. on FS2.

Because of time constraints in the early evening, IndyCar Series qualifying on Saturday will be in its traditional "road course" knockout qualifying format that will culminate with the "Firestone Fast Six" and the battle for the NTT P1 Award.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: World Cup Kicks Off A Pivotal Decade Of World Championships In U.S.
description: Strategic advisor Samuel Hymes looks back at the 2026 World Cup and forward to what could be a pivotal decade of international sporting events in the United States.
fullText:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup turned out to be one memorable event, but it was hardly a stand-alone global extravaganza.

As it turns out, the quadrennial tournament is positioned to kick off a pivotal decade of international sporting championships in the United States, says strategic advisor and Harvard Fellow Samuel Hymes.

He noted that the U.S. faces an unprecedented opportunity, and if the powers that be do the right things, mostly off the playing field, it could go a long way in helping what he calls sports diplomacy.

"The recently introduced American Decade of Sports Act reflects a growing recognition that these events should not be treated as isolated spectacles, but as part of a longer national strategy," Hymes said recently, which he also wrote in a paper looking at the future.

Over the next eight years, the U.S. will host several major sporting world championships. Here is the impressive list of events:

* 2027 Military World Games (for military sportspeople) in Charlotte, N.C.

* 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in Los Angeles

* 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Salt Lake City

A sixth world championship is expected to be added to the list by FIFA at its Extraordinary Congress in Zurich, Switzerland on Nov. 23. The U.S., along with co-hosts Mexico, Costa Rica, and Jamaica, are the lone candidates.

Sports diplomacy, which is essentially soft power, can go a long way in helping a country solidify better relationships with the rest of the world.

"That strategy matters because the benefits could be far greater than ticket sales and television ratings," Hymes stated. "If handled well, this decade of sports could help the country strengthen global relationships, improve public diplomacy, attract investment and tourism, support American business, expand cultural influence, and build people-to-people ties that outlast any single event. In a moment when America's image abroad is often filtered through political polarization and geopolitical competition, major sporting events offer a different kind of stage—one where competence, openness, and cultural confidence can speak louder than official messaging."

Before this year's tournament, which was co-hosted by Mexico, Canada and the USA, Hymes stated that "the World Cup is one of the few events powerful enough to shape how a nation is seen in real time."

Hymes felt that the 2026 World Cup was a prime example. Due to the exorbitant ticket price controversy that dominated headlines before the tournament, there was much trepidation about how the World Cup would be received by the U.S. and the rest of North America.

A record 6,810,966 spectators attended games in 104 matches in 16 venues across the USA, Mexico and Canada.

"I think people can take a sigh of relief that the World Cup was a resounding success," Hymes said. "Prior to the World Cup, for my research, many media were afraid to even talk about this World Cup, even from specific sports publications. They actually spoke more about the World Cup leading into Qatar 2022. But the one about our backyard made a lot of us very nervous, specifically. So, I think after looking back, this is so exciting. And I love how we're already talking about the excitement of 2038, which I think just shows how great and how excited we are."

Hymes meant there has been talk of the U.S. hosting the 2038 World Cup, three cycles down the road. But we'll deal with that in a while.

Beyond Spain winning its second World Cup behind an impressive, new-look defense that was almost impossible to crack, Hymes felt that the biggest victories came off the playing field.

Many cities embraced teams, and foreign spectators embraced many cities. For example, Algerian, Argentine, and English fans were welcomed by the citizens of Kansas City, and the states of Kansas, and Missouri.

Visiting fans sometimes stole the show and headlines with their conduct and enthusiasm. Whether it was a march to the game, invading or taking over Times Square in New York City by the dozens or hundreds, or the Scottish supporters drinking Boston dry, some of the most entertaining and unforgettable moments came well off the pitch.

During and after games, Norway's fans performed the Row With Me routine, which the team recreated after the final whistle. And who was beating the drum? Team leader Erling Haaland.

"It's just everything, even from players really embracing the American culture," Hymes said. "I think Haaland really embraced Texas. He was one of the people that really embraced the American culture the best."

And speaking of culture, Hymes said the halftime show at the final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. on July 19 turned out to be a success. Halftime for players usually lasts around 15 minutes. The halftime show lasted 27 minutes.

Madonna, Shakira, BTS and Justin Bieber were among the performers.

"The halftime show was really something that very traditional soccer fans were worried about," he said. "But now I think that's going to be something that's going to happen again moving forward because of how powerful it was. It had the great Ronaldinho and Ronaldo. You had Madonna there. I think it's going to be something that's going to be more of a demand for the next time they have it."

Hymes added the three host countries worked seamlessly together before and during the competition. The U.S. was home to 11 venues, Mexico three and Canada two.

"I thought we were able to work really well together," he said. "It definitely helped. Especially there is no better tool than sport to connect other countries. I know in the past there may have been other places of poor relationships, but this really brought all three countries together. Especially at the end when we had all the leaders handing out the medals. I think it was really symbolic of a great relationship that is going to progress moving forward."

U.S. President Donald Trump, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney handed out medals at the final.

The World Cup also enabled Americans to learn a little more about the world.

The surprising success of Cape Verde turned many heads. The African side drew their three group stage matches. That included playing eventual champion Spain to a scoreless draw. Cape Verde also made Lionel Messi and Argentina sweat before succumbing in extra time in the Round of 32. An expanded World Cup, from 32 to 48 teams, allowed Cape Verde to compete in the tourney for the first time.

"Cape Verde is one of the exciting, great stories from having more teams in the World Cup," Hymes said. "Many people did not know where it was on the map. They made a strong presence. It's such an inspirational story. It's one of the feel-good stories. More countries were able to be on center stage in the world, and people wanted to learn more about their country."

The U.S. Men's National Team's success also helped the World Cup reach a higher level, and Americans bonded while watching the team, whether it was at home or at Fan Fests. Hymes attended Fan Fests at the National Mall in Washington, D.C. and noted the capacity crowds and passionate responses. The U.S. team won twice in the opening round for only the second time in cup history, and recorded three victories in a tournament for the first time, while reaching the knockout round. The USA, however, was eliminated by Belgium in the Round of 16, in a 4-1 loss.

"I loved seeing the United States national team play together," Hymes said. "You can see the passion throughout the group stage. I think it really was symbolic of how to build the country better from a soccer perspective. Soccer has been the most played sport since the 70s by the youth. But because we have all these different options, people stray away from it. People were coming to different destinations to not only see the games but to be outside the stadiums, go to FIFA fan cities with FIFA Fan Zones to watch them on a larger screen."

When FIFA awarded the U.S. the 1994 World Cup in 1988, the U.S. Soccer Federation needed to create a First Division after the tournament. In 1996, Major League Soccer debuted with 10 teams. It has grown to 30 clubs.

Asked what the impact of the 2026 event could have on American soccer, Hymes replied, "I think it's going to show players from overseas that we have a serious fan base here, especially players that are not leaving. They might not be in their prime, but they're still exciting. They want to come here when they're considering they have all these great options and places to go."

FIFA reportedly will make in the neighborhood of $15 billion from the World Cup. Hymes felt that U.S. Soccer should get some of the money back.

"Absolutely, I think it should go back to the host country," he said. "I think that's very important because we want to grow the game here and make it more of a priority. We have more options in other countries. We have football, basketball, track and field, baseball and all the other sports that we are dominant in.

"If FIFA made billions of dollars, we should get some of those billions too."

And about the 2038 World Cup. There's talk of the tournament returning to the USA sooner than expected.

"Well, no country should have it back-to-back years," Hymes said. "I think the best part about the game of soccer is it's global, and it should go to other countries as well. We are currently in the third-longest drought in our country's history of not hosting a global sporting event. The last event we had was the Salt Lake City Olympics in 2002. Because we're in the new decade of sport, it's a great and perfect timeline from this World Cup to the next one.

"It also has shown that projections show that soccer is going to be even more popular at the time. It's going to be even more of an exciting time."

With 2038, however, we're getting just a bit ahead of ourselves over the next decade. Hymes stated that with the six and perhaps seven big-time sporting tournaments that the U.S. will host, the next 10 years present a unique opportunity that cannot be missed.

"This is what makes the American decade of sports such an important national opportunity," he added. "At its best, it could help the United States modernize how it thinks about public diplomacy, strengthen coordination between government and the sports industry, create economic and civic benefits in host communities, and project a more confident and connected image to the world. It could also encourage the country to treat sport not as a distraction from serious affairs, but as one of the arenas in which serious affairs now play out.

"But that outcome is not automatic. A decade of major events only becomes a national advantage if the country has the imagination to see sport as part of a broader strategic agenda. That is the challenge embedded in the American Decade of Sports Act and in the larger conversation [I'm] trying to bring into the mainstream. The World Cup is the beginning, not the end. The question is whether the United States is ready to use this opening moment to build something bigger - for its global standing, its economy, and its sense of national purpose."

Michael Lewis, the sixth recipient of the Clay Berling Media Career of Excellence Award in 2025, can be followed on X an Bluesky at @Soccerwriter. His 10th soccer book, Around the World Cup in 40 Years: An American sportswriter's perspective, has been published.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Cardinals rookie OL Chase Bisontis tears MCL
description: Cardinals second-round offensive guard Chase Bisontis will miss most, or possibly all, of his rookie season.
fullText:
Cardinals second-round offensive guard Chase Bisontis will miss most, or possibly all, of his rookie season.

NFL Media reports that an MRI revealed a torn MCL for Bisontis, which will require surgery.

The Cardinals listed Bisontis as the second-team right guard, but he was competing with Isaiah Adams for the starting job.

A Raiders defensive lineman fell into the side of Bisontis' left knee in the third quarter on Thursday night, and he was carted to the training room.

The Cardinals have not had good luck with rookie offensive linemen in the preseason.

Last year, sixth-round pick Hayden Conner missed most of the regular season after he was injured in the preseason. In 2024, fifth-round pick Christian Jones missed most of the regular season after he was injured in the preseason. In 2023, fourth-round pick Jon Gaines missed his entire rookie season with a preseason injury.

title: Commanders' Marcus Mariota exits preseason game vs Dolphins with injury
description: Quarterback Marcus Mariota exited the Commanders' preseason opener versus the Miami Dolphins with an apparent injury.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders chose not to start quarterback Jayden Daniels for their preseason game against the Miami Dolphins, opting to start backup Marcus Mariota instead. However, shortly after the game started, Mariota appeared injured and went to the locker room.

Mariota handed the ball off to running back Kaytron Allen when he came up limping even though he was not touched. The injury potentially could have occurred on the play before when he took a shot after delivering a 22-yard pass to wide receiver Dyami Brown. Mariota was later spotted heading to the locker room with the assistant head athletic trainer Mark McCracken.

Marcus Mariota non contact injury on handoff. Watch him top left. He’s out of the game.

Was patting his knee when trainers came out. pic.twitter.com/aBDhMWHTL7

In the four offensive snaps Mariota was on the field before suffering his injury, his only completion was the 22-yard pass to Brown. He only had two passing attempts. Rookie quarterback Sam Hartman replaced Mariota and led the Commanders to their first points of the preseason with a 29-yard field goal from kicker Jake Moody.

The severity of Mariota's injury is unclear at this time. Hartman and fellow rookie Athan Kaliakmanis are the other two quarterbacks the Commanders have on their roster for the rest of this preseason game. This should shed some light on Washington's QB3 battle that has been brewing in training camp between Hartman and Kaliakmanis.

title: Microsoft Is Combining Its Two 'Copilot' Apps (and Ditching These Three Features)
description: Microsoft will now have only one Copilot app for all users.
fullText:
Microsoft Copilot is a little messy. Unlike ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, the company's AI service isn't one universal product. Instead, there's "Copilot," the AI for consumers, directly competing with the aforementioned AI apps; and "Microsoft 365 Copilot," the AI for professional use in Microsoft's work suite. Unless you're totally immersed in Microsoft's AI culture, you might be understandably confused about Copilot, and what features and plans belong to which version of the AI. Luckily, you don't need to be confused any longer.

This week, Microsoft announced its intentions to merge its Copilot and Microsoft Copilot 365 platforms into a single app. If you use Copilot as you would ChatGPT or Gemini, you'll use this app. If you use Copilot with Word and Excel for work or school, you'll use this app. Essentially, if you're using Microsoft's AI for any reason, this will be the app of choice. It might not seem particularly impactful for anyone who uses only one version of Copilot, but if you have to bounce between Copilot and Microsoft Copilot 365, you'll understand the immediate benefits of avoiding two different Copilot apps on screen at once, as The Verge highlights.

As Copilot and Microsoft Copilot 365 are two different experiences, the changes you'll see in the new Copilot app will depend on the app you currently use. Microsoft Copilot 365 users should only have to update their existing app, and Microsoft says users can expect minor navigational changes when switching over. There's also a new app icon, as well as direct access to Copilot chat from the new app.

Copilot users who use Microsoft's AI with their personal account seem to have the most changes to look out for. You should expect to move over to the new app on desktop, but mobile users should be able to switch via an app update. Either way, Microsoft says your chats and content will move over with you. If you use both apps, all your chats and content will merge into the new app, though each will be tied to the specific account you created them with.

Perhaps the biggest news here is what isn't carrying over to the new app. Microsoft says it's ditching three legacy Copilot features as part of this transition: Podcasts, Deep Research, and Group Chat messages. Microsoft will discontinue all three on Aug. 18, so you don't have much time to continue using them.

If you use Copilot's Group Chat feature, make sure to copy any messages or images from your chats before that deadline, as chats will no longer be accessible after Aug. 18. The same goes for Podcasts: You won't be able to generate new podcasts, nor will you be able to access your generated podcasts after the deadline, so export them ahead of time. Any reports you made using Deep Research will be accessible after Aug. 18, but you won't be able to use the feature unless you are a Microsoft 365 Premium subscriber.

You don't have to look far to find replacements for these features. Google's "Gemini Notebook" (formerly NotebookLM) can create AI-generated podcasts for you, and just about every other major AI platform offers its own Deep Research feature. That said, Microsoft isn't the only one retiring features: OpenAI shuttered its AI video generator, Sora, earlier this year, as well as ChatGPT Atlas, its short-lived AI browser. It seems Microsoft is particularly focused on consolidating its AI offerings, seeing as the company has also been removing "unnecessary" Copilot features from Windows.

title: 10 Gboard Hacks Every Android User Should Know
description: There's a lot more to the keyboard than swipe gestures and themes.
fullText:
Gboard is the default keyboard option for a staggering number of Android smartphones across the globe, and it's not just limited to Pixels. If you have an Android device, you've probably used Gboard for years without giving it a second look. The default setup is good, the predictive text suggestions work, and in a pinch, you can swipe to type.

But like other seemingly basic Android apps and features, a lot more is hiding behind Gboard's surface simplicity. Explore the menus, tweak the settings, and learn some gestures, and you'll uncover a ton of useful features that can make it faster and easier to use—without switching to an entirely new keyboard. Here are my favorite tips, tricks, and hacks for Gboard.

You don’t need to go looking for ad-filled clipboard manager apps on Android: Gboard is hiding a capable clipboard manager in plain sight, but it’s not enabled by default. In the Gboard app, tap the Menu button and choose the Clipboard option. On your first try, enable the feature. Now you will see all your copied items here in a handy list. Gboard automatically deletes clipboard entries every hour (a nice security feature), but you can pin any and every entry in the clipboard using the long-press menu. Once pinned, the entry will stay put. You can use this feature to copy and paste items you use frequently, like email templates or your mailing address.

If you’re an Android power user, or if you manage your business or college work via your Android smartphone, you might want a faster way to input long strings of text. On Mac and Windows, you might be familiar with text expansion features and apps. Gboard for Android offers something similar, only it’s called Personal Dictionary for some reason.

Here, you can add any custom phrase and an associated shortcut. The shortcut, when entered, will show the expanded phrase in the suggestion bar. Go to Gboard Settings > Dictionary > Personal Dictionary and tap the Plus button to add a new phrase.

The Backspace (or Delete) key on the Pixel isn’t static. If you swipe left from the backspace key, you’ll start to delete entire words, instead of just letters. Similarly, you can move the cursor around using the space bar: Hold the space bar and move your finger left or right to precisely move the cursor around. And if you want to avoid switching views to enter symbols, just hold the Period (dot) key to reveal the full symbols keyboard. Swipe to the symbol you wish to enter, let go, and you're done.

If you need to enter numbers on Gboard, you can go two ways about it. First, there is a hidden gesture, where you flick keys to enter alternative symbols. So if you swipe down on the letter “e”, it will type in the number “3” instead. Super handy, and can be enabled from Settings > Preferences > Flick keys to enter symbols.

But if you type numbers all the time, nothing can beat a dedicated numbers row to Gboard (though that will take up extra space). From Preferences, you can enable the Number row to get quick access to the number keys.

Tap the Menu button in the Gboard keyboard, and choose the One-handed option. You will now see a smaller keyboard, tucked to one edge. You can tap the Arrow button to change the docking position. You can also tap the Edit button to freely move and resize the keyboard (make it smaller or bring it closer to the bottom edge).

If you don’t like the default size for the Gboard keyboard, you can shorten it, or choose to have it take up half of the screen, with larger keys. Tap the Menu button in the Gboard toolbar, and choose the Resize option. Now, you can drag the handlebar to make the keyboard taller or shorter (you can’t change the width in this feature).

On a big-screen phone or an Android tablet, trying to enter text while seeing what's under the keyboard can be a hassle, especially if you're using multi-app view. But Gboard doesn't have to be docked to the bottom of the screen. From the Gboard Menu, tap the Floating button to detach the keyboard. Now, you can grab the handlebar to move it across the screen to wherever you want. You can also resize the keyboard to make it smaller.

On a computer, text editing is easier and faster. You have arrow keys to move around, a mouse for precise selection, and shortcuts for copying and pasting. Google might have realized this gap on smartphones and tablets, which is why the Text Editing feature in Gboard's Menu exists: When triggered, it replaces the keyboard with big buttons dedicated to selecting and manipulating text.

The new keyboard features a big directional pad with arrows, and a Select button right in the middle. You can use the arrow to move the cursor letter by letter, or press and hold to jump between words. Once the text is selected, use the Cut, Copy, and Paste buttons to manipulate text without ever having to fiddle with long-press gestures or swipes on the screen.

Emojis are kind of boring in 2026, and picking the right GIF feels like an enormous task. Gboard's Emoji Kitchen is somewhere in between. Go to the Emoji tab in Gboard, select two emojis, and Google combines them into a unique emoji sticker. You'll see multiple pairing options so you can choose the one you like.

Pasted in some text that you now need to delete? Don't do the text selection dance. Instead, use Gboard's built-in Undo button. Tap the Menu button, and you should see Undo in the features list. To make this habit stick, add the button to the toolbar by tapping the Edit button, and dragging the Undo button to the top toolbar. Save the arrangement, and now you have a dedicated undo/redo button in easy reach.

title: 10 Screenshot Hacks Every iPhone User Should Know
description: Taking a screenshot on your iPhone can be so much more than just pressing two buttons.
fullText:
While the Mac has the best screenshot tools of any Apple device, it's not quite the same story on iPhone. Your iOS device is mostly restricted to built-in tools for taking screenshots and screen recordings, which makes it hard to bypass apps that block those features. Having said that, your iPhone's screenshot tool is anything but basic, supporting editing, annotations, and even extracting text from images. If you want to take better screenshots on iOS, these 10 hacks can help.

I've always found it unintuitive to take screenshots using hardware buttons on a device with a touchscreen. There are two easy ways to avoid pressing those buttons to take screenshots. The first one relies on a virtual Home button, which you can enable by going to Settings > Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch. From here, enable AssistiveTouch to add a virtual Home button to your iPhone. Next, tap Customize Top Level Menu, then, if you're only interested in using this option for screenshots, reduce the number of icons from six to one by tapping the minus button. From here, tap the remaining icon on this settings page. Go to Device > Screenshot, and tap the blue checkmark in the top-right corner. The next time you tap the virtual Home button, your iPhone will immediately take a screenshot.

The second method uses Back Tap, an iOS feature that triggers various actions when you physically tap the back of your iPhone. You can enable this by going to Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Back Tap. Select either Double Tap or Triple Tap, and go to Device > Screenshot. I recommend picking Triple Tap to avoid accidental screenshots. Once you enable this, tap the back of your phone thrice to take screenshots.

When someone sends you a screenshot of a ticket, or if you've saved an image that mentions a date or time, you can add it to your calendar with a hidden iOS feature. Once you open the screenshot, tap the small Live Text button in the bottom-right corner. (Its icon has three horizontal lines surrounded by dotted borders.) This will reveal a date or time in the bottom-left corner of the screenshot. Tap that button, and you'll see a new page where you can quickly add the event to your calendar. Sometimes, you may see a "More" button next to the identified date or time. This appears when there are multiple dates in a screenshot, and you can tap "More" to select the correct one for your calendar entry. Your iPhone can also identify flight numbers in screenshots and show you the current status of that flight.

This is one of the best features for people who want to avoid piling up useless screenshots in their photo libraries. Once you capture a screenshot on your iPhone, tap the thumbnail to open the screenshot editor page, and tap the checkmark icon in the top-right corner. Here, you can select "Copy and Delete" to save the screenshot to your clipboard and delete it from your device. You can now paste it in other apps, such as Mail, Messages, or WhatsApp. Goodbye, clutter.

Your iPhone comes with a powerful text extraction tool that lets you copy text from images. Just take a screenshot, tap the thumbnail in the bottom-left corner, and hit the Live Text button in the bottom-right corner. This tool instantly identifies all kinds of text in an image, and, from there, you can select and copy it easily.

When I'm annotating a screenshot, I'll often draw a quick squiggle to highlight something to others who'll view it. Since I'm no Picasso, my attempts at drawing a circle (or any other shape) over an element in the screenshot look hopelessly amateur. Fortunately, iOS has a feature that allows you to turn your squiggles into regular shapes. Try this: Draw your best estimation of a circle, rectangle, square, or another shape on a screenshot. Immediately after, hold the screen, and iOS will convert your drawing into a neat symmetrical shape.

I've seen way too many screenshots with poorly hidden bits of sensitive information. When people do this using an iPhone, they often use the pen tool or even the highlighter to hide email addresses, phone numbers, or names. It's surprisingly easy to bypass these methods for those in the know, leaving your info vulnerable. If you're trying to securely hide info in an image, use opaque shapes instead. It's a built-in tool on your iPhone that hides information thoroughly, and is much faster than scribbling over text hundreds of times. When you take a screenshot, open the image via its thumbnail, and tap the pen icon up top. Hit the + button in the bottom-right corner, and tap Add Shape. Choose any shape you like, and tap the first circle in the popover menu to add any color. This will make it an opaque shape. Now, drag this shape over sensitive information and save the image.

Deleting a bunch of screenshots by hand is a pain. However, you can use Apple's Shortcuts app to create an automation to do the job for you. The basic logic behind this automation is to find all photos that are screenshots taken in a specific time period, and delete them in one shot. For most people, this will work as a periodic cleanup tool that deletes recently taken screenshots. As an example, you can use it to delete all screenshots taken in the past 30 days. I've created a sample shortcut for you to follow. You can modify it to suit your needs, but if you use it as is, it'll find and delete all screenshots from the past month. It does ask for confirmation before deleting screenshots, and even after it's done, you can still recover photos from the Recently Deleted folder.

This might be how screenshots work on your iPhone: You take a screenshot, and the device shows a thumbnail in the bottom-left corner. This disappears in a few seconds, and saves the screenshot to your library. If you accidentally take a screenshot and don't tap the thumbnail fast enough, you'll have to manually delete the screenshot from your library. If this bothers you, then I recommend enabling full-screen screenshot previews. That way, the moment you take a screenshot (accidental or not), you'll see a preview, and you can decide if you want to keep the image.

Apple has since changed this default, so there's a chance your screenshots now open in full-screen already. However, if your iPhone is still running with the thumbnail method, you can set this up by going to Settings > General > Screen Capture and enabling Full-Screen Previews.

In addition to screenshots, you can take screen recordings of your iPhone as well. There are many uses for this, but one of the best is to create a screencast. I use this often to help my parents solve tech problems. You can also add microphone audio to these screencasts to make them even more useful, and to avoid recording a voiceover separately. To do this, open Control Center by swiping down from the top-right corner of the screen. In case you don't see the screen recording button here, you can add it by tapping the + button in the top-left corner, and selecting Add a Control > Screen Recording.

Hold the screen recording button until you see a pop-up menu. Tap the "Microphone Off" button, and it'll change to Microphone On. Tap Start Recording, wait for three seconds, and the screen recording will begin. You can now start speaking, and your voice will be a part of your screen recording.

If you want to take screenshots with maximum efficiency, try Screenshot, a screenshot shortcut I found on Reddit. This shortcut bypasses all screenshot previews and capture sounds, and instantly saves your screenshot to a library of your choice. Once you install this shortcut, review its steps, and select an album for your screenshot. (It drops your screenshots in the Recents album by default, which may not be ideal for everyone.) From here, open Control Center, tap the + button, select Add a Control > Shortcut. Now select the Screenshot shortcut, and you're good to go. The next time you want to capture a screenshot as fast as possible, run this shortcut from the Control Center, and you'll notice that it's the least intrusive screenshot workflow. You could even link this shortcut to Back Tap gestures for even faster access.

title: How to Tell If That Apple 'Threat Notification' Is Legit
description: Check push notifications against system settings to verify.
fullText:
Threat actors are always finding ways to make their attacks seem more believable—often by using urgent security matters that push victims to act quickly—so you should always be skeptical of messages and notifications warning you that your device or account has been compromised. That said, if you receive a spyware warning from Apple via push notification, it's likely real, and you shouldn't ignore it.

Apple's threat notification system is designed to alert individuals who have been targeted by mercenary spyware, such as Pegasus, which can silently infect devices and track everything a user does. Since 2021, the company has sent these alerts multiple times a year. In the vast majority of cases, those affected are in high-profile positions—such as politicians, journalists, and activists—that are at a high risk of being targeted. That means the average user is unlikely to ever receive one of these notifications, so it's important to understand how they work and be able to identify what's legitimate and what's not.

According to Apple's support document, threat notifications are now being distributed via push notifications to affected users' iPhones. These alerts will appear on the Lock Screen and in Settings. Users will also receive an email alert to the address linked to their Apple Account sent from [[email protected]]. (Previously, Apple sent alerts via email and Messages.) Lock Screen alerts will have a red warning icon and read "Apple Threat Notification: Apple detected a mercenary spyware attack targeted at your iPhone. There are actions you can take now to help protect your data and your device."

If you receive a push notification or an email that appears to be from Apple, you should take it seriously and also verify it in your device Settings and Apple Account dashboard, as scammers may try to capitalize on this by sending fake alerts that impersonate Apple. When you go to Settings on your iPhone, you'll see an Apple Threat Notification menu just below your main profile. Then, log into account.apple.com—there will be a banner at the top of the page labeled "Threat Notification" with a link to view additional details.

Legitimate threat notifications from Apple will never require you to click links, download files, install apps, or provide credentials by email or phone. If you're urged to do any of these things, it's a scam. You should be especially wary of security-related notifications if you're not a high-risk iPhone user who is likely to be targeted.

That said, affected users are advised to follow Apple's recommended steps to protect themselves. This may include turning on Lockdown Mode, an OS-level security setting that severely limits iPhone features in order to block malicious actors from gaining access. If you receive an Apple threat notification, you can also contact Access Now's Digital Security Helpline, which is available 24/7, for assistance.

title: Judge refuses to block Trump administration from building border wall along tribe's reservation
description: A federal judge refused on Friday to block the Trump administration from taking steps to build 62 miles of international border wall along part of a Native American tribe's reservation without its con...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge refused on Friday to block the Trump administration from taking steps to build 62 miles of international border wall along part of a Native American tribe's reservation without its consent.

U.S. District Judge Richard Leon in Washington, D.C., denied the Tohono O'odham Nation's request for a court-ordered halt to border wall construction on its 2.8-million-acre reservation. Leon ruled the tribe hasn't established that a border wall will change its reservation boundaries without congressional authority.

The judge also rejected the tribe's claim that the planned border wall would illegally trespass on its reservation.

"And in any event, I find that the Government's interests in securing the border, enforcing immigration laws, and ensuring public safety outweigh any surviving irreparable harms at this juncture," Leon wrote.

A tribe spokesperson didn't immediately respond to an email seeking comment on the decision.

The O'odham reservation in the Sonoran Desert in Arizona abuts 62 miles of the Mexico border. The tribe has over 37,000 members, including thousands who live in Mexico.

Building the border wall would led to "significant devastation" on the reservation, including the destruction of mountain peaks that are sacred to the O'odham, tribe attorneys said.

"It would fray the ties between O'odham communities and families on opposite sides of the border, interfere significantly with O'odham religious rituals and practices, and destroy plant and animal resources sacred to the O'odham," the lawyers wrote.

In 1907, President Theodore Roosevelt issued a proclamation reserving a 60-foot strip of public land along the U.S.-Mexico border for a buffer zone called the "Roosevelt Reservation," which was formed a decade before the reservation's establishment.

Tribe attorneys say it is "fanciful at best" to suggest that border wall construction can be confined to a 60-foot-wide corridor.

During a July 22 hearing, Leon appeared to be skeptical that U.S. laws tip in favor of the tribe's bid for a preliminary injunction, calling it an "extraordinary" request. Leon, who was nominated to the bench by Republican President George W. Bush, said he couldn't find a previous court ruling under comparable circumstances.

"This is a novel case with novel issues," the judge said.

title: Rising golf star, 18, dies after brain haemorrhage
description: Promising Australian golfer Jessica Bang dies at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage as she prepared for a tournament in Thailand.
fullText:
Jessica Bang, a promising Australian golfer, has died at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage.

Bang, who won her first professional event in just her fifth start earlier this year, was preparing for a tournament in Thailand on 1 August when she collapsed.

She was rushed to a hospital in Bangkok and had emergency brain surgery. After being in intensive care for nearly two weeks, she died on Thursday.

The WPGA Tour of Australasia said Bang, who turned professional at the end of 2025, was an "outstanding young talent".

"The thoughts and prayers of everyone at the WPGA Tour of Australasia and the broader Australian golf community are with Jessica's family, friends and all those who knew and loved her at this incredibly difficult time," a statement read.

Writing on a GoFundMe page that was set up by Bang's cousins after her collapse, family members said: "We are truly heartbroken by this news.

"The funds we have raised will be given to her parents to help contribute towards her medical expenses."

Bang qualified to start her rookie season in the WPGA last November.

She shot a final-round 65 to win a regional qualifying event in February to reach the NWS Women's Open on the Ladies European Tour, where she missed the cut.

title: Notts and Durham reach One-Day Cup semi-finals
description: Jack Haynes and Kyle Verreyne hit centuries as Notts beat Yorkshire in the One-Day Cup quarter-finals, as Durham also win through.
fullText:
Nottinghamshire pulled off a glorious comeback as they and Durham both won away from home to book their places in Sunday's One-Day Cup semi-finals.

Notts looked out for the count when they slumped to 1-3 chasing Yorkshire's 273-9 at Clifton Park, York - including two wickets in two balls for Ben Coad.

But, from 55-4, a 154-run stand between centurions Jack Haynes (116*) and Kyle Verreynne (105) transformed the contest and they went on to win by three wickets with eight balls to spare.

Notts, who have never reached the final of this competition since it moved from Lord's to their Trent Bridge home in 2021, now face an East Midlands derby in Sunday's semi against Group A winners and 2024 winners Leicestershire.

Durham's David Bedingham-inspired 162-run humbling of Lancashire at Old Trafford earned the visitors their seventh successful passage to a List A semi-final.

They will now play Group B winners Middlesex, who qualified automatically for a home semi with ease, winning seven of their eight group games.

The match will be played at Radlett, as Lord's is unavailable.

Durham were far too good for Lancashire as they recovered from a slightly sticky start to post a powerful 349-8 from their 50 overs.

Approaching halfway, Durham - including former England skipper Ben Stokes - were only on 110-3, but Bedingham (104) and Ollie Robinson (76) then shared a crucial stand of 149 in 16 overs.

Even when they were parted in the 41st over on 259-4, Durham still plundered a further 90 runs.

Stokes hit his second ball for six before being caught by Australian Marcus Harris at long off for 11, but Bedingham went on to complete his fifth hundred in all formats against Lancashire off just 87 balls before some late hitting from Colin Ackermann and captain Kasey Aldridge.

In reply, former Durham man Keaton Jennings and Josh Bohannon briefly looked in control - but both departed before Harris lucklessly removed a bail by treading on his stumps.

It was not Rocky Flintoff's day either as he departed for 22, one of four wickets for leg-spinner Shaq Ghafari as the hosts were bowled out for 187 to suffer the fifth heaviest defeat in their illustrious 63-year one-day cricket history.

Teenager Joe Moores - the nephew of Notts and former England head coach Peter Moores - was their mainstay, hitting four sixes in his 51 off 42 balls.

"Credit to Ollie Robinson," Bedingham told BBC Radio Newcastle. "He changed the game when he came in.

"I always thought 350 would be a tough chase. It put pressure on Lancashire. The bowlers were excellent and it was a fine all-round team effort."

"We were out-performed by Durham in all departments," Lancs head coach Steven Croft told BBC Radio Lancashire. "The toss was pretty important but we probably took a couple of backward steps.

"They batted well but, at halfway they probably had 30-40 runs over par and they carried that momentum forward. We didn't throw too many punches in that run chase. Rocky and Moorsey sort of showed the way."

An excellent first-team best score of 91 from youngster Will Bennison was the cornerstone of Yorkshire's 273-9, but it maybe should have been more as they lost momentum in mid-innings.

And, ultimately, it did not prove quite enough as in-form South African Verreynne came in to help Notts from their stuttering start with 105 off 123 balls.

After he was out, Haynes carried on the fine work as the former Worcestershire man got his side over the line with only his third List A century.

His former Pears team-mate Dillon Pennington, who had earlier struck four times with the ball, assisted at the end with two fours and a six in his 18-ball cameo of 22.

Earlier, after starting with the wickets of Freddie McCann and visiting skipper Haseeb Hameed, Coad claimed a fine 5-52 - but how different it might have been if Verreynne had not survived the hat-trick ball.

Notts, who last won a List A trophy at Lord's in 2017, now have a chance to follow Worcestershire as the latest winners of the trophy, while Yorkshire, who have lost their last eight semi-finals, must wait another year to try and end their long wait for a first List A final since they won the old C&G Trophy in 2002.

Haynes, who was playing his first game since July because of injury, told BBC Radio Nottingham: "It would obviously be nice to have a carrot of a home final, but we've got a big game ahead of us first on Sunday at Grace Road.

"From the position we were in, we dragged it back brilliantly with the ball from the start they got.

"No matter how long it's been, you always think, 'Have I forgotten how to bat or not?' So, it was nice to hit a couple out of the middle. And Kyle, with his class, made it a lot easier for me."

Yorkshire head coach Anthony McGrath added: "We would have bowled had we not lost the toss. We knew it was probably going to get easier. We were in a great position, 194-3 with about 12 overs left. Really, we should have got 300. That would probably have been enough."

title: Virginia Man Argues His 'FTP&ATF' License Plate Is Free Speech. The Supreme Court Might Hear His Case.
description: A federal appeals court ruled that Curtis Whateley's anti-police vanity plate was private speech protected by the First Amendment. Virginia says it will seek review from the Supreme Court.
fullText:
A Virginia man's anti-police license plate is at the center of what could be a landmark First Amendment case, following a federal appeals court ruling in his favor last month.

Virginia motorist Curtis M. Whateley says he has a free speech right to keep his customized license plate, which reads "FTP&ATF," an abbreviation that foul-mouthed puzzle-solvers will decipher as "Fuck the police and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms." The State of Virginia argues that it has the right to revoke Whateley's plate because license plates are government-owned, not a public soapbox. The state says it's going to take its case to the Supreme Court.

The case highlights a niche, often amusing, but still consequential issue in First Amendment law: whether a vanity license plate is private or government speech.

The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in 2015 that Texas could deny a group's application for a specialty license plate design showing the Confederate flag. Most U.S. district courts and state courts interpreting the decision have held that, while government-run vanity plate programs are a nonpublic forum, the specific character combination of the plate is private speech, which restricts the government from censorship based on viewpoint.

But until the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit issued an opinion on Whateley's case on July 31, no federal appeals court had ruled on the matter, according to the American Civil Liberties Union of Virginia (ACLU-VA), which is representing Whateley. The three-judge panel unanimously found Virginia's personalized license plate messages are private speech subject to First Amendment protection.

"There is no doubt that Virginia has final approval authority over the messages Virginia's drivers wish to convey on their vanity plates, and that it may deny approval for messages it believes to be vulgar or offensive," the 4th Circuit panel wrote. "But the exercise of that authority, on its own, is more consistent with the regulation of private expression in a public forum than it is with the government speaking on its own behalf."

Matt Callahan, a senior supervising attorney at the ACLU-VA, said in a press release that the 4th Circuit's ruling "goes beyond Mr. Whateley, reaffirming these protections for the almost one million drivers in Virginia who have exercised their free speech rights through personalized license plates."

"The First Amendment is a foundational American principle created specifically to ensure that the government cannot silence people for speech it does not agree with," Callahan said.

According to his lawsuit, Whateley ordered and received his customized license plate without any problems in 2023. But in May of 2024, the Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) received an anonymous complaint that Whateley's license plate was "offensive."

The next month, the Virginia DMV's Personalized Plate Review Board voted to recall Whateley's plate because it violated rules forbidding messages that were "profane, obscene, or vulgar in nature" or "used to condone or encourage violence."

Whateley filed a First Amendment lawsuit against the Virginia DMV commissioner, arguing that his personalized plate was private speech expressing his political opinions.

A lower district court dismissed Whateley's suit last year, ruling that the state's personalized license plates aren't subject to ordinary First Amendment scrutiny because they are government speech.

The 4th Circuit ruling vacated that decision and remanded Whateley's case back to the district court. The court could still rule against Whateley, but Virginia's arguments for censorship will be subjected to a much higher bar.

Virginia doesn't want to have to meet that bar in Whateley's case or any number of future First Amendment lawsuits. A spokesperson for the Virginia attorney general told The New York Times following the ruling that the state would ask the Supreme Court for review.

"The commonwealth has a responsibility to ensure that state-issued license plates are not profane and do not promote dangerous hate speech or incite harm," the spokesperson said.

Attempting to conflate anti-government rhetoric with hate speech is a common censorship tactic by federal, state, and local governments.

In any case, similar bans have mostly fared poorly in court. In 2024, a federal judge struck down Delaware's rules governing vanity plates for unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination; the plaintiff in that case was a breast cancer survivor whose application for a "FCANCER" plate was first approved and then recalled for offensiveness.

Over the last decade, similar rulings have come down against censorious state DMVs in California, Kentucky, and South Dakota. In 2016, Maryland's Court of Appeals held that, "Although mindful that we risk being haunted by the spirit of the late comedian and social commentator George Carlin…the characters or message on a vanity license plate represent private speech in a nonpublic forum."

And in 2014, New Hampshire's ban on vanity plates that were "offensive to good taste" was struck down after being challenged by a man whose application for a "COPSLIE" vanity plate was rejected.

However, not all courts have ruled in favor of drivers. The Tennessee Supreme Court ruled last year that personalized license plates are government speech and not subject to the First Amendment's ban on viewpoint discrimination.

At the center of the case was plaintiff Leah Gilliam's personalized Tennessee license plate, "69PWNDU," which she held for more than a decade before the state revoked it in 2021 on the grounds that it "referred to sexual domination," according to the Tennessee Supreme Court opinion. (The number 69 is a popular reference to a sex position. "PWNDU" is short for "pwned you," ancient video game slang for "owning" or defeating an opponent.)

The Indiana Supreme Court is one of the only others that has ruled that license plates constitute government speech.

The post Virginia Man Argues His 'FTP&ATF' License Plate Is Free Speech. The Supreme Court Might Hear His Case. appeared first on Reason.com.

title: Arteta not worried about Arsenal contract talks
description: Mikel Arteta says supporters "don't have to worry about" his future at Arsenal as he wants to extend his contract and the time left on his deal is "not an issue".
fullText:
Mikel Arteta has said that supporters "don't have to worry about" his future at Arsenal as he wants to extend his contract and the time left on his deal is "not an issue".

The Gunners boss is into the final 12 months of his agreement that he signed in 2024 but says he is relaxed about formal talks taking place regarding a renewal.

Arteta has been in charge of Arsenal since 2019 and led the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season.

Arsenal face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday (15:00 BST) and Arteta was asked in his news conference about the concern some supporters may have given he is yet to agreed a new deal before the 2026-27 campaign kicks off.

"No, they don't have to worry about any of that because I want to be here, I'm extremely happy," Arteta said.

"I feel very grateful to work with the people that I work with and whenever we have the possibility we will resolve that and that's it."

The Gunners are attempting to build on their success of last season and strengthen their squad in the transfer window.

They were unsuccessful in their pursuit of Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr but have signed midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, Greece international winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge and made Piero Hincapie's loan move from Bayern Leverkusen into a permanent transfer for a combined £143.5m.

Goalkeeper Illan Meslier has also arrived on a free transfer from Leeds United while, from last season's squad, Leandro Trossard, Jakub Kiwior and Christian Norgaard have been moved on.

The Gunners remain interested in Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa or Jarell Quansah of Bayer Leverkusen as a further defensive reinforcement in the market following injuries to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber.

With the transfer window open until 1 September, the feeling at the club is that finalising a contract can come at a quieter period in the season.

"There's always another priority I think and that's the way we've been treating it. Arteta added.

"I think because everybody feels comfortable that the time on the contract is not going to be an issue.

"I think because my will certainly is to be here and I'm very happy here.

"And my feeling from the club is is the same one so I think that's why everybody doing it things in a really organic way."

Arsenal also reached the Champions League final last season where they were beaten by Paris St-Germain and Arteta has repeatedly spoken of his ambition since that loss to take the Gunners to next level.

"I'm not going to talk about any individuals, obviously what I can tell you is the ambition of the club." Arteta said.

"It's big that we want to improve the squad, we want to evolve the squad in order to achieve that.

"We have obviously detected some areas that they can be strengthened and that's what we are trying to do."

title: Castleford shrug off coach problems to beat Hull
description: Castleford Tigers put their coaching problems aside as they beat Hull FC at the MKM Stadium to record only their third Super League away win of the season.
fullText:
Tries: Batchelor, Barron, Martin Goals: Sezer

Tries: Atoni, Ravalawa, Hood Goals: Weaver 3

Castleford Tigers put their coaching problems aside as they beat Hull FC at the MKM Stadium to record only their third Super League away win of the season.

Boss Ryan Carr remains absent for personal reasons and former Huddersfield Giants number one Luke Robinson is cutting short a holiday to take training on Monday as their new assistant boss.

Cas, though, overcame all their difficulties as they scored tries through Renouf Atoni, Mikaele Ravalawa and Liam Hood and claimed the victory late on after trailing 14-12.

Hull were on a high after announcing Aussie legend Daly Cherry-Evans' arrival next season but fell short, despite scoring through Joe Batchelor, Harvey Barron and Lewis Martin.

Castleford showed great professionalism in the face of all their off-field issues to score from their first attack after nine minutes when Atoni crashed over from close range through two Hull tackles, with Tom Weaver adding the two points.

The try spurred Castleford on and they deservedly added a second on 26 minutes, passing the ball along the line for winger Ravalawa to power over in the right-hand corner.

Hull were denied a score to haul themselves back into the game when Barron intercepted a pass and ran 90 yards to touch down, only for referee James Vella to rule it out for a late tackle by Batchelor.

Castleford added to the indignity when Weaver kicked a penalty to stretch the lead to 12-0 before the home side finally hit back four minutes before the interval.

This time Batchelor was the hero as he grounded Jake Arthur's grubber kick, with Aidan Sezer adding the extras.

Hull continued their comeback in the 47th minute, thanks to another Arthur kick, and this time Davy Litten knocked it back for Barron to collect and crash over to cut Castleford's lead to just two points.

The Tigers were creaking under pressure and the Black and Whites took the lead for the first time in the match when Martin went over in the left corner after 59 minutes for his fifth try in his last four games against Castleford.

To their immense credit, back came Castleford and hooker Hood managed to burrow his way over the line in the 68th minute to restore their lead, with Weaver kicking the two points to extend the lead.

They move up to ninth in the table, four points clear of Hull in 12th.

Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told BBC Radio Leeds:

"I thought we were the best side. We showed some real toughness, some real resilience and some real fight, which is probably what we've been lacking these last few weeks.

"I'm pleased for the boys after a real tough week and I'm just really proud of them because it's a hard place to come.

"I think the pressure was off, coming away from home, we could play without fear.

"They were always going to come back at us and I just liked the response when they scored, the response from the players and Hoodie came up with a big play to get us over the line."

Hull FC interim coach Andy Last told Sky Sports:

"Yeah, a disappointing result, a disappointing performance.

"We can find a reasonable level for periods in games, like we did against St Helens. Tonight, we didn't start particularly well. We got rolled far too easily up the field and then when we did build a little bit of momentum at the start of the second half, it became a real stop-start affair.

"So, yeah, disappointed with the result, disappointed with the performance, it's just not good enough.

"There's been a lot of talk about next year, but you know I've got a job still this year and what we've served up today in terms of consistency, it's nowhere near good enough."

title: Departing Romero says he wasn't perfect at Spurs
description: Cristian Romero says he "wasn't perfect" during his five-year stint at Tottenham Hotspur as he prepares to complete a move to Atletico Madrid.
fullText:
Cristian Romero has said he "wasn't perfect" during his five years with Tottenham Hotspur.

The Argentina centre-back is set to complete a move to Atletico Madrid after they agreed to pay Spurs £34.2m for the 28-year-old.

Romero's last game for Tottenham was against Sunderland in April, when he left the field in tears with a knee injury that would rule him out of Spurs' last six Premier League games.

The team were in a relegation battle and Romero upset fans by planning to be in Argentina for their final game, to watch his first club Belgrano play in the Primera Division Apertura final.

He ultimately returned to England to attend Spurs' 1-0 win over Everton, which meant they stayed up and finished 17th for a second consecutive season.

"I know I wasn't perfect," Romero posted on X., external "But one thing gives me peace: I always gave everything. I defended this shirt with pride and with all my heart."

Romero joined Tottenham from Atalanta in 2021 and became a mainstay in their defence, making 156 appearances.

His best moment with Spurs was helping the club win their first trophy in 17 years as they beat Manchester United in the 2025 Europa League final.

"When I arrived, I had a clear dream: to leave my name in this club's history," Romero added.

"I knew the only way was through hard work, sacrifice and achieving something that had seemed so difficult for so long: lifting a trophy again. And we did it.

"I'm leaving the club, but a part of my heart will always remain here. Once I was one of you. Today, I leave as one of you forever.

"With all my love and respect. Thank you for everything."
